docs.text: HardFOC product firmware Vortex V1 firmware ¶ The ESP-IDF application for the HardFOC Vortex V1 motor controller: it boots the board through the Vortex HAL, supervises its health and is becoming a CiA 402 CANopen drive node with one object dictionary as its source. Get started See the architecture What the device is ¶ Vortex V1 drives one motor. An ESP32-C6 runs this firmware and commands a TMC9660, which closes the current, velocity and position loops itself. The firmware brings the board up, watches it and exposes it on CAN. Board wiring, pin maps and the managers live in the Vortex V1 HAL documentation . Single-axis motor controller Vortex V1 HardFOC MCU ESP32-C6 (RISC-V, single-core FreeRTOS); flash configured as 2 MB in sdkconfig Motor controller TMC9660, UART by default or SPI, on-chip FOC loops Sensors AS5047U angle encoder slot, BNO08x IMU, NTC on TMC9660 AIN3 I/O PCAL95555 expander, CAN (TWAI) port, WS2812 status LED Firmware ESP-IDF v5.5, C++17, project version 2.0.0 ( CMakeLists.txt ) Status Bring-up: boot, supervisor and HAL demos run; the CANopen device is being rebuilt to the design What you get ¶ A thin app_main and one orchestrator task with an ordered, table-driven boot ( architecture ). A fixed set of tasks with known stacks and priorities ( threads ). A supervisor that checks HAL health every 5 s and never moves the motor on a timer ( safety ). An optional CANopen device on the CAN port: CANopenNode over the generated dictionary, tested in CI against a host build of the same node ( CANopen ). One YAML object dictionary that generates the CANopenNode tables, the EDS, C++ and Python constants and the object dictionary reference . Host-tested contracts for the CiA 402 state machine, fault policy, frame routing and parameter store ( testing ). Four tasks over one HAL Figure description and sources From top to bottom. The ESP-IDF main task runs app_main, which starts the VortexSys orchestrator task and waits for its boot table, then becomes the supervisor loop. VortexSys brings up the HAL, starts the LedDemo thread (WS2812TestThread) and, when menuconfig selects the CANopen device, the co_svc task that serves CoNode (CANopenNode over the generated object dictionary, on the TWAI port). Every task reaches the hardware through the Vortex HAL singleton, which owns the managers, the hf-core handlers and the chip drivers. Stack sizes and priorities are the constants in the sources listed below. Four tasks over one HAL Figure description and sources From top to bottom. The ESP-IDF main task runs app_main, which starts the VortexSys orchestrator task and waits for its boot table, then becomes the supervisor loop. VortexSys brings up the HAL, starts the LedDemo thread (WS2812TestThread) and, when menuconfig selects the CANopen device, the co_svc task that serves CoNode (CANopenNode over the generated object dictionary, on the TWAI port). Every task reaches the hardware through the Vortex HAL singleton, which owns the managers, the hf-core handlers and the chip drivers. Stack sizes and priorities are the constants in the sources listed below. Drawn from: main/app_main.cpp ; main/apps/system/sub_threads/VortexSystemThread.h ; main/apps/system/sub_threads/VortexSystemThread.cpp ; main/apps/node/sub_threads/ws2812/WS2812TestThread.h ; main/apps/node/canopen/CanopenDevice.cpp ; main/apps/node/canopen/CoSvcFreeRtos.cpp ; main/apps/supervisor/VortexSupervisor.cpp ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/firmware-tasks.py . Layers ¶ Layer Where What it owns Application main/ app_main , the orchestrator, the supervisor, worker threads Contracts contracts/ Header-only rules (CiA 402, fault policy, routing, store codec, OD ids); no RTOS, no HAL; host-tested, not yet linked into the firmware Object dictionary od/ vortex_od.yaml and everything tools/odgen generates from it HAL hal/hf-hal-vortex-v1 (submodule) The Vortex singleton, managers, hf-core handlers, chip drivers, CANopenNode ( HAL docs ) Platform ESP-IDF v5.5 FreeRTOS, drivers, the build system The application is the ESP-IDF main component. The root CMakeLists.txt adds only the HAL to EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS ; the HAL builds hf-core and the drivers itself. There is no middleware layer: anything shared lives in the HAL. Source map ¶ Path Role main/app_main.cpp IDF entry: logger, start the orchestrator, wait for boot, run the supervisor main/apps/system/sub_threads/VortexSystemThread.{h,cpp} vortex_app::VortexSystemThread : the boot table and Step() main/apps/system/api/VortexSystemStateMachine.{h,cpp} vortex_app::VortexSystemStateMachine : the coarse lifecycle state main/apps/supervisor/VortexSupervisor.{h,cpp} RunVortexSupervisorLoop() : health checks, status logs, HAL demos main/apps/node/sub_threads/ws2812/ WS2812TestThread (task LedDemo ) main/apps/node/canopen/ The CANopen device: CoNode , FrameRouter , the co_svc task and CanopenDevice , built only when menuconfig selects it ( CANopen ) main/utils/vortex_demos.h Declarations of older demo functions; nothing implements them main/Kconfig.projbuild The HardFOC Vortex main (app) menu Boot table ¶ VortexSystemThread::Setup() walks kInitSequence in order. A failed step marked recoverable is logged and boot continues; a failed non-recoverable step moves the state machine to Fault , tears down the steps that completed, in reverse order, and makes Setup() return false. Step Recoverable Setup Teardown vortex_hal no Vortex::GetInstance().EnsureInitialized() Vortex::Shutdown() ws2812 yes EnsureInitialized() and Start() of the LedDemo thread Stop() can_worker yes With menuconfig None : nothing. With CANopen device : StartCanopenDevice() on vortex::bsp::esp32c6::CanController() StopCanopenDevice() Adding a step means adding a Setup* / Teardown* pair and a row to kInitSequence[] in VortexSystemThread.cpp . Boot and updates follows the whole sequence from reset. System state machine ¶ VortexSystemStateMachine holds one atomic VortexSystemState and the reason of the last change. TryTransition() stores the new state without a guard table; the states mark milestones for logs. From To When (start) Boot Setup() starts Boot HalInit the vortex_hal step HalInit ThreadsUp the can_worker step ThreadsUp Ready every step done HalInit Fault a non-recoverable step failed Ready Fault Cleanup() Supervisor loop ¶ After boot, RunVortexSupervisorLoop() runs on the ESP-IDF main task and does not return. It prints a banner, the ESP-IDF version, chip information and Vortex::GetSystemDiagnostics() , then loops every 100 ms: Period Counter condition Work 2 s count % 20 == 0 Toggle the status LED between STATUS_OK and STATUS_BOOT 5 s count % 50 == 0 Vortex::PerformHealthCheck() ; LED STATUS_WARN on failure, STATUS_OK otherwise 10 s count % 100 == 0 Log uptime and free heap; log whether LedDemo runs 20 s count % 200 == 0 GPIO (pulses GPIO_EXT_GPIO_CS_1 high for 200 ms, reads PCAL GPIO17/18), ADC and temperature reads, LED (four status animations, 0.5 s each) 20 s, offset 10 s count % 200 == 100 Motor controller, IMU and encoder demos: handler lookups, device counts, encoder angle and velocity (reads only) The demos address pins and channels by their HAL names ( GPIO_EXT_GPIO_CS_1 , ADC_TMC9660_AIN3 ); the names are in the HAL pin map . Design choices ¶ A thin app_main . Boot order and teardown live in one table that can be read top to bottom. Static stacks. VortexSystemThread and WS2812TestThread pass member arrays to CreateBaseThread() ; only CANopenNode allocates ( CO_new() and an 8192-byte task stack). One owner per bus direction. Only one task may drain BaseCan::ReceiveMessage() on the CANopen bus, which is why the CAN worker is a menuconfig choice with one option at a time. Rules before integration. The CiA 402 and fault tables are written and host-tested in contracts/ before the firmware uses them ( design notes ). Next: Threads .

docs.text: Boot and updates ¶ What happens from reset to the supervisor loop, what makes the board reboot, and how firmware gets onto it. From reset to the supervisor ¶ sequenceDiagram participant M as main task (app_main) participant O as VortexSys participant H as Vortex HAL M->>M: Logger::Initialize() M->>O: EnsureInitialized(), Start() activate O O->>H: [1/3] vortex_hal: EnsureInitialized() O->>O: [2/3] ws2812: start LedDemo O->>O: [3/3] can_worker: none, or start the CANopen device (co_svc) O-->>M: IsSetupComplete(), BootSucceeded() deactivate O M->>M: RunVortexSupervisorLoop() (never returns) app_main initialises the logger, so every later step can log. It creates the VortexSys task ( EnsureInitialized() ) and starts it ( Start() ). Setup() runs on that task, not on the main task. The main task waits until IsSetupComplete() is true, for at most ComputeVortexBootTimeoutMs() = 120 000 ms. It checks BootSucceeded() , which Setup() sets only after the last step. It enters RunVortexSupervisorLoop() . By then the HAL is initialised and the workers run. The architecture page lists the boot steps and what each one tears down. When the board reboots ¶ app_main calls ResetWithDiagnostic() , which logs FATAL: <reason> — rebooting in 2000 ms with tag MAIN , waits 2 s and calls esp_restart() , in four cases: Reason in the log Cause VortexSystemThread EnsureInitialized failed The orchestrator task could not be created VortexSystemThread Start failed The task could not be started VortexSystemThread Setup did not complete in time Setup() took more than 120 s VortexSystemThread boot sequence failed vortex_hal failed: the HAL did not initialise The ws2812 and can_worker steps never cause a reboot; their failures are logged as warnings and boot goes on. The task watchdog (5 s, idle task) can also reset the chip; see Threads . Flash layout ¶ Setting Value ( sdkconfig ) Flash size 2 MB ( CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASHSIZE_2MB ), DIO Partition table ESP-IDF single app, partitions_singleapp.csv ( CONFIG_PARTITION_TABLE_SINGLE_APP ), offset 0x8000 App rollback off ( CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE not set) Firmware updates ¶ There is no over-the-air update today: the single-app partition table has no second app slot, and nothing in main/ calls the OTA API. Update the firmware over USB with idf.py -p PORT flash , or flash the build/*.bin files from the fw-release-v5.5-* artifacts CI keeps for 14 days. The CANopen node design moves to a two-OTA partition table to prepare firmware download over CANopen (CiA 302-3, objects 0x1F50 / 0x1F51 ); the protocol itself is out of scope for that design. Next: Safety .

docs.text: CANopen ¶ The CANopen side of Vortex V1: the CANopen device on the CAN port, the object dictionary and how it is generated, and the tools that read it. Vortex V1 is a CANopen device (slave): a CiA 301 node that will carry the CiA 402 drive profile. It is not a master for other drives. The CANopen node design is the plan; this page describes the code. What runs today ¶ Piece State Where CANopenNode v4 Compiled into the HAL only with CONFIG_HARDFOC_HAL_CANOPENNODE_SLAVE HAL third_party/CANopenNode CO driver and ports hf-core's generic driver CO_driver_hardfoc.c and the EspTwaiPort binding HAL lib/core/handlers/common/canopen/ CANopen device CoNode , served by the co_svc task; started by boot step can_worker when menuconfig selects CANopen device main/apps/node/canopen/CoNode.cpp , CanopenDevice.cpp Object dictionary in the build The Vortex dictionary generated from od/vortex_od.yaml ( HF_CORE_CANOPENNODE_OD_DIR ) od/canopennode/ Stack configuration SDO block transfer with CRC, configurable EMCY, LSS fastscan, timer-next main/apps/node/canopen/config/hf_co_app_config.h Host node The same CoNode on SocketCAN or the pipe bus, tested by python-canopen in CI host/node , tests/node How a frame travels: Receive. The TWAI RX interrupt hands each frame to a lock-free ring in the CO driver and wakes co_svc . co_svc dispatches the frame to CANopenNode in task context, through the frame router. Transmit. Frames go out with EspCan::TrySendMessage() , which never blocks. A full TX queue leaves the frame pending in its CANopenNode buffer, and CO_CANmodule_process() sends it again. Errors. TEC, REC and bus-off become CANopen EMCY messages, and a bus-off controller gets a recovery request. Router. FrameRouter applies contracts/router_policy.hpp . SDO server 2 (0x1201, virtual COB-IDs 0x6C0/0x5C0 + node-ID) is never reachable from the CAN port. Not here yet Parameter storage (0x1010 / 0x1011) and the NVS LSS record are the next step of the design . After that come the CiA 402 axis and drive_rt , then the fault funnel. Until then, a reset forgets an LSS-assigned node-ID. The node runs on the 1 kHz tick ( Threads ), which still awaits its bench soak. Start sequence ¶ StartCanopenDevice(EspCan&, bit rate) creates the port, the node and the service task. CoNode::Start() then runs, in order: Step Call Values 1 CO_new() Allocates the stack on the heap 2 CO_CANinit() The CO driver instance with the EspTwaiPort in the CAN slot; bit rate from CommChannelsManager::GetCanBitRate() (500 kbit/s) 3 CO_LSSinit() LSS address from 0x1018; pending node-ID and bit rate 4 CO_CANopenInit() Node ID CONFIG_VORTEX_CANOPEN_NODE_ID (or the LSS-assigned one); first heartbeat 500 ms; SDO server timeout 1000 ms; NMT startup from 0x1F80 (bit 2 = 0, the default, waits for an NMT start) 5 CO_CANopenInitPDO() PDOs from the dictionary 6 CO_CANsetNormalMode() , task co_svc 6144-byte stack, priority 17; woken by received frames and by CANopenNode's timer-next, at least one tick per wait CO_ERROR_NODE_ID_UNCONFIGURED_LSS is accepted in steps 4 and 5, so an unconfigured node (ID 255) can be set up with LSS. NMT reset communication repeats steps 2 to 6. NMT reset node restarts the chip. The object dictionary ¶ One YAML file, od/vortex_od.yaml , is the source of every artefact. tools/odgen writes them and CI fails when one is stale: Artefact Path Used by CANopenNode dictionary od/canopennode/OD.c , OD.h the firmware and the host node EDS (CiA 306) od/vortex_v1.eds , also packaged in tools/vortex_canopen CANopen masters and tools C++ identifiers contracts/vortex_od_ids.hpp contracts and host tests Python identifiers tools/vortex_canopen/vortex_canopen/od_ids.py host tools Reference page docs/od-reference.md the Object dictionary page of this site Device field Value Product name HardFOC Vortex V1 Vendor ID 0x00000000 (not registered with CiA yet) Product code 0x00560001 Revision ( 0x1018:03 ) 1.0 od/vortex_od.lock.json records the dictionary hash for each revision: changing the dictionary without bumping device.revision fails the check. python3 -m pip install -r tools/odgen/requirements.txt python3 tools/odgen # regenerate every artefact python3 tools/odgen --check # what CI runs Host tools ¶ Tool What it is tools/vortex_canopen Python package with the generated identifiers and the matching EDS ( vortex_canopen.eds_path() ), the frame-record codec and the pipe-bus python-can interface ( vortex_pipe ); the base of the planned vortex-canopen command line host/node ( vortex_node_host ) The CANopen node built for Linux or macOS, on vcan0 or the pipe bus; see Testing and CI USB-CAN scripts Small python-can scripts that build NMT and expedited SDO frames by hand, for bench checks Next: Configuration .

SDO server 2 (0x1201, virtual COB-IDs 0x6C0/0x5C0 + node-ID) is never reachable from the CAN port. Not here yet Parameter storage (0x1010 / 0x1011) and the NVS LSS record are the next step of the design . After that come the CiA 402 axis and drive_rt , then the fault funnel. Until then, a reset forgets an LSS-assigned node-ID. The node runs on the 1 kHz tick ( Threads ), which still awaits its bench soak.
docs.title: What runs today

docs.text: StartCanopenDevice(EspCan&, bit rate) creates the port, the node and the service task. CoNode::Start() then runs, in order: Step Call Values 1 CO_new() Allocates the stack on the heap 2 CO_CANinit() The CO driver instance with the EspTwaiPort in the CAN slot; bit rate from CommChannelsManager::GetCanBitRate() (500 kbit/s) 3 CO_LSSinit() LSS address from 0x1018; pending node-ID and bit rate 4 CO_CANopenInit() Node ID CONFIG_VORTEX_CANOPEN_NODE_ID (or the LSS-assigned one); first heartbeat 500 ms; SDO server timeout 1000 ms; NMT startup from 0x1F80 (bit 2 = 0, the default, waits for an NMT start) 5 CO_CANopenInitPDO() PDOs from the dictionary 6 CO_CANsetNormalMode() , task co_svc 6144-byte stack, priority 17; woken by received frames and by CANopenNode's timer-next, at least one tick per wait CO_ERROR_NODE_ID_UNCONFIGURED_LSS is accepted in steps 4 and 5, so an unconfigured node (ID 255) can be set up with LSS. NMT reset communication repeats steps 2 to 6. NMT reset node restarts the chip.
docs.title: Start sequence

docs.text: Configuration ¶ Every switch that changes what this firmware does: the menuconfig options, the committed sdkconfig values and the compile definitions. menuconfig ¶ idf.py menuconfig shows two menus that belong to Vortex. HardFOC Vortex main (app) ( main/Kconfig.projbuild ): Option Values Default Effect VORTEX_APP_CAN_BOOT_WORKER (choice) VORTEX_APP_CAN_BOOT_CANOPEN_SLAVE , VORTEX_APP_CAN_BOOT_NONE NONE Which task drains the CANopen bus at boot. CANopen device also compiles CoNode , FrameRouter , CoSvcFreeRtos and CanopenDevice VORTEX_CANOPEN_NODE_ID 1 to 127 1 Node ID passed to CO_CANopenInit() and CO_CANopenInitPDO() HardFOC Vortex HAL (in the HAL submodule): Option Default Effect HARDFOC_HAL_CANOPENNODE_SLAVE off Compiles CANopenNode, hf-core's CO driver and EspTwaiPort into the HAL, with the Vortex OD; the app's CANopen device choice depends on it To try the CANopen device: enable HARDFOC_HAL_CANOPENNODE_SLAVE , then pick CANopen device under CAN RX drain worker at boot , and set the node ID. Read the CANopen limits first. Committed sdkconfig ¶ The repository commits a full sdkconfig . The values the firmware depends on: Setting Value Why it matters CONFIG_IDF_TARGET esp32c6 The only target CONFIG_FREERTOS_UNICORE y One core for every task CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ 1000 1 ms tick; hf-utils-rtos-wrap and pdMS_TO_TICKS delays resolve to 1 ms. Also set in ci/sdkconfig.canopen ; see Threads CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_STACK_SIZE 3584 Stack of the supervisor loop CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_TIMEOUT_S 5 Task watchdog, idle task checked CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_UART_BAUDRATE 115200 Console on UART0, USB Serial/JTAG secondary CONFIG_LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL 3 (info) CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASHSIZE 2MB CONFIG_PARTITION_TABLE_SINGLE_APP y No OTA slot; see Boot and updates CONFIG_COMPILER_OPTIMIZATION_DEBUG y -Og for ESP-IDF; main adds -O2 Compile definitions ¶ Define Set in Scope HARDFOC_VORTEX_V1=1 , HARDFOC_VORTEX_API=1 root CMakeLists.txt every component ESP_IDF_VERSION_MAJOR=5 , ESP_IDF_VERSION_MINOR=5 root CMakeLists.txt every component HARDFOC_MAIN_APPLICATION=1 , HARDFOC_VORTEX_API_MAIN=1 main/CMakeLists.txt main only LOG_LOCAL_LEVEL=ESP_LOG_INFO main/CMakeLists.txt main only main builds as C++17 with -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter -Wno-missing-field-initializers -O2 -g . The project version is 2.0.0 ( PROJECT_VER in the root CMakeLists.txt ). Adding a source file to main ¶ Put it under main/apps/ or main/utils/ . Add it to MAIN_SRCS in main/CMakeLists.txt (inside an if(CONFIG_...) block if a menuconfig option gates it). Add a new header directory to INCLUDE_DIRS . Add a new ESP-IDF component to REQUIRES or PRIV_REQUIRES . Next: Troubleshooting .

docs.text: Getting started ¶ Build the firmware with the ESP-IDF version CI uses, flash it to a Vortex V1 board and read the boot log. The board drives a motor Bring a new board up on a current-limited bench supply with the motor unloaded. The firmware does not command motion on its own, but the HAL demos talk to the TMC9660 every 20 s. Requirements ¶ Item Version or value Where it is set ESP-IDF v5.5 (CI builds with the release-v5.5 image of espressif/idf ) .github/workflows/build-and-analyze.yml Target esp32c6 sdkconfig ( CONFIG_IDF_TARGET ), workflow IDF_TARGET CMake 3.16 or newer (ships with ESP-IDF) CMakeLists.txt Git with submodule support the HAL is a submodule Board Vortex V1, USB-C for flash and console The root CMakeLists.txt also defines ESP_IDF_VERSION_MAJOR=5 and ESP_IDF_VERSION_MINOR=5 , so build with a 5.5 release. Steps ¶ Install ESP-IDF v5.5 for the ESP32-C6 and open a shell with its environment: mkdir -p ~/esp && cd ~/esp git clone -b release/v5.5 --recursive https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf.git cd esp-idf && ./install.sh esp32c6 && . ./export.sh The ESP-IDF extension for VS Code installs the same thing through its setup wizard. Clone the firmware with its submodules. The HAL ( hal/hf-hal-vortex-v1 ) brings hf-core, the chip drivers and CANopenNode with it: git clone https://github.com/hardfoc/hardfoc-vortex-v1.git && cd hardfoc-vortex-v1 git submodule update --init hal/hf-hal-vortex-v1 git -C hal/hf-hal-vortex-v1 submodule init git -C hal/hf-hal-vortex-v1 config submodule.docs/hf-development-handbook.update none git submodule update --init --recursive The HAL's docs/hf-development-handbook submodule is private; the third line skips it, as CI does. With access to it, git clone --recursive is enough. Build. The repository commits its sdkconfig , so the target is already esp32c6 : idf.py build idf.py menuconfig opens the options described in Configuration . Flash and open the console (115200 baud on UART0, with USB Serial/JTAG as the secondary console): idf.py -p PORT flash monitor What the boot log shows ¶ Tag Lines Meaning MAIN Spawning VortexSystemThread... app_main started the orchestrator VortexSys Boot: 3 init steps , then [1/3] vortex_hal , [2/3] ws2812 , [3/3] can_worker the boot table runs VortexSys CAN worker disabled (menuconfig: none) the default: no CANopen task VortexSys Boot complete — state=... every non-recoverable step passed MAIN Boot complete. Main task entering supervisor loop. the supervisor takes over VortexMain banner, ESP-IDF version, chip information, system diagnostics printed once VortexMain System Status - Uptime: ... every 10 s, demos every 20 s steady state A FATAL: ... rebooting in 2000 ms line from MAIN means a boot step failed; see Troubleshooting . Other useful targets ¶ Command What it does idf.py -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug build The Debug build CI also runs idf.py size-components Flash and RAM use per component (CI keeps it as an artifact) idf.py fullclean Remove build/ after an ESP-IDF or submodule change Next: Architecture .

docs.text: Hardware ¶ The board this firmware runs on, in one table, and where its wiring is documented. The Vortex V1 HAL documentation is the reference for the board: block diagram, every pin, the buses and the managers that own each chip. This firmware never uses a pin number; it calls the HAL by name. docs.text: Safety ¶ What stops the drive from doing harm today, what is only designed, and the rules to follow on the bench. Nothing here is safety-rated Vortex V1 has no certified safety function (no STO, no SS1). The CANopen node design is safety-aware, but lists CiA 402-4 functional safety as a non-goal. What the firmware does today ¶ Mechanism Where Effect No motion from the firmware main/apps/supervisor/VortexSupervisor.cpp The supervisor reads the motor controller, IMU and encoder; it never enables or moves the motor on a timer. Motion is reserved for the CiA 402 state machine of the CANopen device HAL must initialise boot step vortex_hal , not recoverable If the HAL fails, the completed steps are torn down and the board reboots after 2 s Health check every 5 s Vortex::PerformHealthCheck() Failure sets the status LED to STATUS_WARN and logs System health check failed! Task watchdog CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_TIMEOUT_S=5 , idle task checked A starved idle task resets the chip TMC9660 protection the TMC9660 itself The chip has its own overcurrent, supply and temperature protection; nothing in main/ changes its settings CAN off by default menuconfig CAN worker None The firmware neither sends nor answers on CAN unless you select the CANopen device Rules already written and tested ¶ The rules the CANopen device will enforce exist as header-only tables in contracts/ , with host tests that run in CI. The firmware does not use them yet. Contract Header Host test CiA 402 power drive state machine, transitions 0 to 16 contracts/cia402_rules.hpp tests/host/test_cia402_rules.cpp Fault policy: cause to EMCY code, error register and reaction, with escalation contracts/vortex_fault_policy.hpp tests/host/test_fault_policy.cpp Frame routing and wireless authority rules contracts/router_policy.hpp tests/host/test_router_policy.cpp Parameter store record format contracts/od_store_codec.hpp tests/host/test_od_store_codec.cpp What the design adds ¶ The CANopen node design describes the rest; the sections to read: Topic Section Liveness requirements for motion 5.5 Safe defaults and limit enforcement 6.2 Fault funnel and EMCY mapping 6.4 Safety arbiter and liveness-gated watchdog (500 ms, fed only while critical threads are live) 6.5 Wireless safety rules 7.4 On the bench ¶ Use a current-limited supply and an unloaded motor until the configuration is proven. Know the node ID before you send NMT or SDO frames: a valid sequence enables a CiA 402 drive. With the CANopen device selected, read the threads note on the 1 kHz tick first: its bench soak (no task-watchdog trip) has not been run yet. The bench documents linked from the HAL hardware page cover the first spin of a motor on the TMC9660. Next: CANopen .

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ What runs on every pull request, how to run the same checks on your machine, and what is still tested only on the bench. Host tests (contracts) ¶ The headers in contracts/ build and run on a PC with sanitizers ( tests/host , preset host-debug : Debug, ASan and UBSan, Ninja): cd tests/host cmake --preset host-debug cmake --build --preset host-debug ctest --preset host-debug Test Covers test_cia402_rules.cpp The CiA 402 rule table ( contracts/cia402_rules.hpp ) test_fault_policy.cpp The fault policy table ( contracts/vortex_fault_policy.hpp ) test_router_policy.cpp Router policy and authority rules ( contracts/router_policy.hpp ) test_od_store_codec.cpp The parameter store record codec ( contracts/od_store_codec.hpp ) test_od_ids.cpp The generated identifiers ( contracts/vortex_od_ids.hpp ) The build also compiles every contracts header on its own ( vortex_contracts_standalone ), so a header that misses an include fails. Object dictionary checks ¶ git submodule update --init hal/hf-hal-vortex-v1 git -C hal/hf-hal-vortex-v1 submodule update --init third_party/CANopenNode python3 -m pip install -r tools/odgen/requirements.txt python3 tools/odgen --check VORTEX_REQUIRE_CANOPENNODE = 1 python3 -m pytest -q tools/odgen/tests Test Covers test_cli.py --check passes on the tree, fails on any drift, and enforces the revision bump test_schema.py The YAML schema rules test_eds.py python-canopen loads the EDS; every object matches the YAML; export and re-import keep every object test_canopennode_layout.py The CANopenNode example EDS through odgen reproduces the example OD.c / OD.h test_od_c_build.py The generated OD.c builds with CANopenNode v4 and CO_CANopenInit accepts it odgen supports Python 3.10 and newer; CI uses 3.10. CI workflows ¶ Workflow Jobs Runs on host.yml ( CI • Host tests ) contracts-host , od-drift , node-host , CI gate (green only when all are) every pull request, push to main build-and-analyze.yml ESP-IDF build in release-v5.5 , Release and Debug, plus a Release build with the CANopen device on ( ci/sdkconfig.canopen ), with size report and firmware artifacts; cppcheck on main/ ; CodeQL; actionlint pull requests to main , push to main docs.yml ( Docs ) Strict site build, link check, Lighthouse, screenshots; publish to GitHub Pages from main pull requests to main , push to main The CANopen node on the host ¶ host/node builds vortex_node_host : the firmware's CoNode , FrameRouter , generated OD.c and CANopenNode, with hf-core's LinuxSocketCanPort ( --port vcan0 ) or PipePort ( --port pipe:<path> , a UNIX-socket hub carrying frame records). tests/node runs python-canopen against it ( design §9.4 ): git -C hal/hf-hal-vortex-v1 submodule update --init lib/core third_party/CANopenNode cmake -S host/node -B build/node-host -G Ninja && cmake --build build/node-host python3 -m pip install -r tests/node/requirements.txt python3 -m pytest tests/node # vcan0 if present, else the pipe bus (VORTEX_BUS=vcan0|pipe) Suite Checks test_nmt_hb.py boot-up, NMT states and addressing, heartbeat period (0x1017), 0x1F80, reset communication and node test_sdo.py expedited 1–4 bytes, segmented, block transfer with CRC (and a corrupted CRC), abort codes, SDO server 2 kept off the CAN port test_pdo.py mapping procedure and aborts, event timer, inhibit time, SYNC TPDO, RPDO into the OD, RPDO length and timeout EMCYs test_lss.py fastscan, node-ID assignment and store across a restart, inquiries, bit-timing table, --nvs path validation test_frame_record.py the Python frame-record codec against the golden bytes of hf-core's C++ codec CI job node-host builds the binary with ASan and UBSan and runs the suites on the pipe bus, then again on vcan0 when the runner can load vcan . On the bench ¶ Nothing runs on hardware in CI. The CANopen node design has the USB-CAN bench plan. Next: Design notes .

docs.text: Threads ¶ Every FreeRTOS task the firmware creates, with its stack, priority, period and owner, read from the sources. The ESP32-C6 runs FreeRTOS on one core ( CONFIG_FREERTOS_UNICORE=y ) with a 1 kHz tick ( CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 ), so every delay is a multiple of 1 ms. Tasks ¶ Task Created by Stack (bytes) Priority Period Source ESP-IDF main ESP-IDF 3584 ( CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_STACK_SIZE ) ESP-IDF default (1) 100 ms supervisor tick main/app_main.cpp , main/apps/supervisor/VortexSupervisor.cpp VortexSys app_main 16384, static 5 Step() every 100 ms main/apps/system/sub_threads/VortexSystemThread.h LedDemo boot step ws2812 4096, static 2 Step() every 20 ms, next animation every 5 s main/apps/node/sub_threads/ws2812/WS2812TestThread.h co_svc boot step can_worker , only with the CANopen device selected 6144, heap 17 woken by received frames; otherwise CANopenNode's timer-next, at least one tick main/apps/node/canopen/CoSvcFreeRtos.cpp What the HAL managers lock, and from which tasks they may be called, is on the HAL threading page . co_svc and the 1 kHz tick co_svc sleeps until a frame arrives or CANopenNode's next deadline, and never less than one tick (1 ms), so CANopenNode timers resolve to 1 ms, as the CANopen node design requires. The 1 kHz tick still needs the bench soak (no task-watchdog trip with the CANopen device selected). The default build (CAN worker None ) does not start this task. Who talks to whom ¶ Producer Consumer Through app_main VortexSys IsSetupComplete() and BootSucceeded() , polled by TestLogicWithTimeout() for up to 120 s Supervisor LedDemo IsThreadRunning() , logged every 10 s Supervisor, LedDemo status LED LedManager : both write it (see Troubleshooting ) TWAI RX interrupt co_svc the CO driver's lock-free RX ring and a task notification co_svc CAN bus EspCan::TrySendMessage() (never blocks); the only RX consumer Watchdog ¶ The task watchdog is on with a 5 s timeout and watches the idle task ( CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_TIMEOUT_S=5 , CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_CHECK_IDLE_TASK_CPU0=y ). No firmware task subscribes to it. Next: Boot and updates .

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms, their causes and the fix, starting with the cheapest check. Symptom Cause Fix CMake stops with Vortex HAL not found at: .../hal/hf-hal-vortex-v1 The HAL submodule is not checked out Run the submodule commands in Getting started Submodule update fails on docs/hf-development-handbook That HAL submodule is private git -C hal/hf-hal-vortex-v1 config submodule.docs/hf-development-handbook.update none , then update again Build errors after switching ESP-IDF version Stale build/ or a shell from another ESP-IDF . $IDF_PATH/export.sh for v5.5, then idf.py fullclean build Filename too long or $GIT_DIR too big on Windows Nested submodules under a long path git config --global core.longpaths true and clone to a short path such as C:\src , or use WSL2 FATAL: VortexSystemThread boot sequence failed The HAL did not initialise Scroll up to the first VortexSys error; the HAL logs which manager failed FATAL: ... docs.text:
Vortex V1 CANopen Device: Design ¶ Status Draft for owner review Date 2026-11-01 Scope Firmware, tooling and verification for a CiA 301 / 305 / 402 CANopen device on the HardFOC Vortex V1 board, with wireless access paths and a CAN FD migration route Code base read hf-hal-vortex-v1@28f1a63 (branch ci/fix-workflows ), hardfoc-vortex-v1@0d98cde (branch ci/fix-workflows ), hf-core@54cbb5e (main; submodules hf-core-utils@2f7e1da , hf-utils-canopen@242a88e , hf-internal-interface-wrap@ba7f5ca ), hf-vortex-driver@68cd06d , hf-tmc9660-driver@bc3cfcc , hf-as5047u-driver@8b4f7a9 , hf-bno08x-driver@9936d27 , hf-pincfg@6b8354d , CANopenNode ac21407 (v4, 2025-11-22) Reference architecture pw-controller-sw (layering, BaseThread run control, rule-table state machines in contracts, safety arbiter, liveness-gated watchdog, host tests) Paths below are relative to the repository named in each section. Mermaid diagrams render on GitHub. 1. Summary ¶ Vortex V1 should become a CiA 402 servo drive node on its CAN port. It should keep one object dictionary (OD), described in a single YAML source. That source generates the CANopenNode OD.c/OD.h , the CiA 306 EDS file, C++ index constants and the Python constants. Every transport carries the same CANopen services against that OD: the TWAI port today, a CAN FD port on a future STM32, ESP-NOW and Wi-Fi. Motion is driven by the TMC9660's own current, velocity, position and ramp loops. The ESP32-C6 runs the CiA 402 state machine, mode logic, limits, the fault arbiter and the communication stack. The repository already has the pieces (CANopenNode v4 as a submodule, a CO_driver shim, managers for every chip), but the current CAN path does not work on hardware (§3). The plan therefore rebuilds the integration rather than extending it. Key decisions: Stack: CANopenNode v4 (Apache-2.0, already vendored) behind a narrow CoStack seam, so a CiA 1301 stack can replace it later without touching application code. Single source of truth: od/vortex_od.yaml generates firmware, EDS, documentation and Python. CI fails on drift. Transport router: one CO_CANmodule that fans out to N ICanPort bindings, with per-port COB-ID policy. Wireless gets its own SDO server channel and read-only mirrors. It never gets motion authority by default. Threads: one SYNC-driven real-time owner thread for SPI2 (TMC9660 + AS5047U). It runs as a short burst at the highest priority. A separate service thread handles SDO, storage and NMT. An I2C owner thread handles the PCAL95555 and BNO08x. A safety monitor gates the task watchdog. The TMC9660's own SPI heartbeat is the independent last-resort stop. Wireless: Wi-Fi with a TLS tunnel that python-can can use as a bus, so the same tools work over Wi-Fi as over USB-CAN. CiA 309-3 ASCII is an optional extra. ESP-NOW is for a USB dongle that bridges to a PC (slcan). It also serves board-to-board links. Verification: the same node application and OD build for Linux and run against vcan0 , or against a pipe bus where vcan is unavailable. They are exercised by pytest and python-canopen against a simulated motor. 2. Goals, non-goals and requirements ¶ 2.1 Goals ¶ G1: A complete, conformant-in-spirit CANopen device on the board's CAN port: CiA 301 NMT, heartbeat, SYNC, TIME, EMCY, SDO (expedited, segmented, block), PDO with runtime mapping, 0x1010/0x1011 store/restore, identity, and CiA 305 LSS. G2: Easy to exercise with a USB-CAN adapter on Windows, Linux or macOS, using a single pip install tool. G3: Motor-agnostic. BLDC/PMSM, stepper and brushed DC, with Hall, ABN, SPI-encoder or open-loop feedback, are selected and commissioned through OD objects. No rebuild is needed. G4: Expose the IMU (BNO08x), the absolute encoder (AS5047U), temperatures, power rails, spare GPIO, expansion slots and the LED. G5: Extra access paths over Wi-Fi and ESP-NOW that use the same OD semantics and never weaken safety. G6: CAN FD on a future STM32 should be a port-binding and stack-configuration change, not an application rewrite. 2.2 Non-goals (this design) ¶ CiA 402-4 functional safety (STO/SS1 certification). The design is safety-aware, but nothing in it is safety-rated. Firmware update over CANopen (CiA 302-3, 0x1F50/0x1F51). The partition layout is prepared for it (§10, step 12). The protocol is deferred. Acting as an NMT master or CiA 402 master for other drives. This is what the current CANOpenBLDCThread does, and it is removed (§10). CANopen safety (SRDO, CiA 304), CiA 302 network management, and Thread/Zigbee on 802.15.4. CiA conformance certification. Conformance- style tests are in scope. Certification needs a CiA vendor ID and a test house (open question Q1). 2.3 Requirements ¶ ID Requirement Owner ask Verified by R1 Node implements CiA 301 services in §2.1 G1 with CANopenNode v4 complete CANopen node host CI conformance suite (§9.4) R2 CiA 305 LSS: node-ID and bit-rate configuration, fastscan, persistent store complete node, USB-CAN test_lss.py , bench R3 CiA 402 state machine (0x6040/0x6041), modes pp, pv, tq, hm, csp, csv, cst; ip reported unsupported in 0x6502 many motors test_402_fsm.py , bench demos R4 OD generated from one source. EDS shipped and identical to firmware OD (CI drift check) USB-CAN usability CI od-drift job R5 vortex-canopen Python CLI over any python-can interface and over the Wi-Fi tunnel USB-CAN usability, wireless CLI smoke tests in CI R6 Motor/feedback catalog rows and commissioning procedures in the OD many motors and feedbacks sim tests + bench matrix R7 IMU, encoder, temperatures, rails, GPIO, LED in manufacturer area with PDO-mappable packed variants expose IMU and expansions test_manufacturer_area.py R8 Every detected fault maps to one EMCY code, error-register bits and a CiA 402 reaction from one table safety table-driven host test R9 Heartbeat-consumer loss, RPDO timeout and SYNC loss trigger the 0x6007 abort-connection reaction safety fault-injection tests R10 0x1010/0x1011 persist to NVS with records keyed by OD address and survive OD layout changes persistence test_storage.py , migration fixtures R11 Wireless transports reach the same OD. Enabling the drive over wireless is refused unless policy allows it wireless, safety test_authority.py R12 Frame type, port capabilities and PDO length checks are FD-ready. No 8-byte assumptions above the port binding CAN FD on STM32 static check + host FD build ( CO_PDO_MAX_SIZE test, §8) R13 1 kHz SYNC with one node at 1 Mbit/s and an RT step ≤ 300 µs WCET on the C6 performance on-target timing histogram object 0x4201 3. What exists today (verified) ¶ Area Fact Evidence CANopenNode v4 submodule at third_party/CANopenNode (commit ac21407 ). Compiled only when CONFIG_HARDFOC_HAL_CANOPENNODE_SLAVE is set hf-hal-vortex-v1/Kconfig , CMakeLists.txt:57-75 , hf-core/cmake/hf_core_build_settings.cmake:460-494 OD The build compiles the upstream example example/OD.c (DS301 profile, 1 SDO server, 4 RPDO, 4 TPDO). It has no CiA 402 or manufacturer objects hf_core_build_settings.cmake:492 , third_party/CANopenNode/example/OD.h:45-48 Storage example/CO_storageBlank.c is compiled, so 0x1010/0x1011 do nothing same file, line 479 Missing stack modules CO_fifo.c , crc16-ccitt.c and CO_gateway_ascii.c are not compiled, and CO_CONFIG_FIFO / CO_CONFIG_CRC16 default to 0. So there is no SDO block transfer and no gateway 301/CO_config.h:706,739 Driver shim hf-core/handlers/common/canopen/CO_driver_vortex.c . Software RX dispatch. CO_CANsend calls the registered TX hook inside portENTER_CRITICAL . The hook ends in EspCan::SendMessage → twai_node_transmit(timeout) + vTaskDelay . That is a blocking call inside a critical section. CO_CANmodule_process is empty, so bufferFull frames are never retried and error-state bits are never reported to the stack CO_driver_vortex.c:16-18,145-178,200 ; CO_driver_target.h lock macros RX path CanopenSlaveRuntime polls BaseCan::ReceiveMessage(m, 0) . EspCan::ReceiveMessage unconditionally returns CAN_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION . The slave never receives a frame. The same applies to CANOpenBLDCThread (via CanOpenBaseCanLink::Read ) hardfoc-vortex-v1/main/apps/node/canopen/CanopenSlaveRuntime.cpp:75 ; hf-internal-interface-wrap/src/mcu/esp32/EspCan.cpp:282-294 ; CANOpenBLDCThread.cpp:114 EspCan RX The RX callback runs in ISR context ( twai_node_receive_from_isr ) and calls the user callback from the ISR. Its conversion error path calls ESP_LOGE in ISR context EspCan.cpp:766-800,952-963 EspCan TX Adds vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(1)) after every successful transmit ("prevent driver overload") EspCan.cpp:262-266 Tick rate (fixed: now CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 , step 1 of §10.2) CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=100 , so pdMS_TO_TICKS(1) == 0 . The slave task loop ( vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(1)) , priority 5) is a busy yield that starves the idle task. CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_CHECK_IDLE_TASK_CPU0=y with a 5 s timeout, so a TWDT trip is likely. (Inferred from config, not bench-verified.) hardfoc-vortex-v1/sdkconfig:1077,1120 ; CanopenSlaveRuntime.cpp:98 Bit rate 500 kbit/s hard-coded in two places CommChannelsManager.cpp:282 ; CanopenSlaveRuntime.cpp:117 Build break VortexSystemThread.cpp includes VortexCanHostThread.h unconditionally, and that file does not exist in any repository apps/system/sub_threads/VortexSystemThread.cpp:2 ; find over all clones BaseCan FD hf_can_message_t has FD flags ( is_canfd , is_brs , is_esi , canfd_dlc ) but data[8] . SetDLC() accepts 64 for FD frames. That is a latent buffer overrun, because the struct only pretends to model FD hf-internal-interface-wrap/inc/base/BaseCan.h:165-235 STM32 StmCan wraps bxCAN or FDCAN. The FD data phase is "requires HAL extensions" inc/mcu/stm32/StmCan.h:3-8 TWAI hardware ESP-IDF documents two TWAI controllers on the C6, classic only. FD frames are treated as errors. There is one mask filter (or a dual 16-bit split). The RX callback runs in ISR context. Vortex routes one controller (TX GPIO14, RX GPIO15) IDF TWAI (C6) ; hf_functional_pin_config_vortex_v1.hpp:95-96 Transceiver standby PCAL_CAN_HS_STB_OP (PCAL95555 P10) is defined, but no code in the HAL or examples drives it. If the transceiver's STB defaults to standby, the bus is silent. Verify against the schematic grep over hf-hal-vortex-v1/lib , examples Host client hf-vortex-driver is NMT plus expedited SDO download only. VortexProtocol.hpp names 0x1021 as "Error behavior". In CiA 301 that object is 0x1029 (0x1021 is Store EDS) inc/vortex/VortexProtocol.hpp:21 Helpers docs/helpers/usb_can/*.py hand-builds frames with python-can (no python-canopen). A __pycache__ directory is committed hardfoc-vortex-v1/docs/helpers/usb_can/ TMC9660 Parameter-mode driver with motor types NONE/DC/STEPPER/BLDC, commutation modes (open-loop V/I, ABN, Hall, SPI encoder), velocity/position sensor selection, ramp, reference search, brake, I²t, protection, stop events and an SPI/UART heartbeat monitor ( HEARTBEAT_MONITORING_CONFIG/TIMEOUT ). Erratum 4: target updates are serviced in a ~1 kHz internal loop hf-tmc9660-driver/inc/tmc9660.hpp:465-5044 , parameter_mode/tmc9660_param_mode_tmcl.hpp:460,1569,1752,2898,5028,5106 ; examples/esp32/main/common/vortex_bench_safety.hpp:169-173 Feedback wiring The AS5047U is on the host SPI2 (CS GPIO20), not on the TMC SPI-encoder port. Hall/ABN need a bootloader BootloaderConfig mux. Closed loop on AS5047U is "static unless wired through SPI-enc on the TMC" examples/esp32/docs/BENCH_MATRIX.md:28-34,63 ; BLDC_BRINGUP.md:19 Expansion EXT_GPIO_CS_1 (GPIO19) and EXT_GPIO_CS_2 (GPIO8) are external SPI2 chip selects. MotorController reserves device slots 2 and 3 for external TMC9660s. EncoderManager / ImuManager have external slots. There is a UART (GPIO⅘), and PCAL95555 bits 0, 7, 8, 9 are unassigned pin map lines 88-131; MotorController.h ( MAX_TMC9660_DEVICES=4 , indices ⅔) Persistence NvsManager exposes namespaces vortex , vortex_cal , vortex_cfg . The partition table is single-app (no OTA) lib/managers/NvsManager.cpp:26-28 ; sdkconfig:597 Version info HAL CMake already generates HF_HAL_GIT_SHA_* macros per submodule hf-hal-vortex-v1/CMakeLists.txt:353-380 Conclusion: keep the CANopenNode submodule, the CMake gate idea, the managers and the TMC9660/AS5047U/BNO08x handlers. Rewrite the driver binding, runtime, OD, storage and tooling. 4. Architecture ¶ 4.1 Layers ¶ The layout follows pw-controller-sw/firmware/README.md . A header-only contracts package holds the shared types and pure rule tables. The HAL owns hardware, the app owns threads, and host tests link only contracts and the app logic. flowchart TB subgraph tools["Host tools (PC)"] CLI["vortex-canopen CLI
(python-canopen + python-can)"] EDS["vortex_v1.eds (generated)"] end subgraph app["hardfoc-vortex-v1 / main (node app)"] NODE["CoNode: CANopenNode instance,
OD extensions, storage, LSS"] DRV["DriveAxis: CiA 402 FSM, modes,
limits, commissioning"] SAF["SafetyArbiter + LivenessMonitor"] WL["Wireless: WiFi tunnel, ESP-NOW, 309-3 (opt)"] ROUTE["FrameRouter (N ports, COB-ID policy)"] end subgraph contracts["hardfoc-vortex-v1 / contracts (header-only, host-tested)"] ODT["Generated OD ids + record types"] FSM["Cia402 rule table, fault policy table,
authority rules, PDO profile tables"] FR["CanFrame (len<=64, FDF/BRS/ESI), port caps"] end subgraph hal["hf-hal-vortex-v1 (board HAL facades)"] AX["AxisPort facade (TMC9660 via MotorController)"] SENS["Encoder / IMU / Temp / Gpio / Led facades"] NVS["NvsManager"] CANP["CAN port binding (EspTwaiPort)"] end subgraph core["hf-core"] BASE["BaseCan v2, BaseSpi, BaseI2c, EspCan/StmCan"] H["Tmc9660Handler, As5047uHandler,
Bno08xHandler, Pcal95555Handler"] COD["CO_driver_hardfoc.c (generic over ICanPort)"] end CLI --> EDS NODE --> ODT DRV --> FSM SAF --> FSM ROUTE --> FR NODE --> ROUTE ROUTE --> CANP WL --> ROUTE DRV --> AX NODE --> SENS NODE --> NVS AX --> H SENS --> H CANP --> BASE NODE --> COD COD --> FR Rules (adapted from pw-hal/README.md "Design rules"): The node app never includes twai.h , EspCan.h or chip drivers. It uses HAL facades ( AxisPort , ImuFacade , …) and the ICanPort interface. Contracts contain no .cpp , no RTOS and no HAL. They hold the CiA 402 transition table, fault policy table, authority rules, PDO profile tables and generated OD identifiers. Host tests use them directly. One bus has one owner thread (see pw-controller-sw/docs/software/threading-model.md §4): SPI2 belongs to drive_rt , and I2C belongs to i2c_io . Hot paths bind once at init. They do no string lookups ( GpioManager::Get(std::string_view) ) per cycle. 4.2 Object dictionary as the single source of truth ¶ flowchart LR Y["od/vortex_od.yaml
(objects, types, access, PDO-mappable,
defaults, limits, units, persist group,
FD max lengths, docs)"] --> G["tools/odgen (Python)"] G --> ODC["OD.c / OD.h
(CANopenNode v4 format)"] G --> EDSF["vortex_v1.eds (CiA 306)"] G --> HPP["contracts/vortex_od_ids.hpp
+ record structs"] G --> PY["vortex_canopen/od_ids.py
+ packaged EDS"] G --> MD["docs/od-reference.md"] G --> XDD["vortex_v1.xdd (CiA 1311, later for FD)"] ODC --> FW["firmware build"] EDSF --> CLI2["python-canopen import_od"] The YAML schema mirrors the CiA 306 attributes: ParameterName , ObjectType , DataType , AccessType , PDOMapping , DefaultValue , LowLimit / HighLimit . It adds: persist: comm|app|cal|none , od_extension: <C++ handler> (dynamic objects served from snapshots), fd_only: bool and units . odgen writes OD.c/OD.h in the exact CANopenNode v4 layout. A CI job cross-checks the output by importing the generated EDS with the pinned CANopenEditor EDSSharp CLI, exporting "CANopenNode V4", and diffing the structural content (entries, sub-counts, attributes). The in-house emitter is primary because it runs anywhere without .NET. CANopenEditor is the independent oracle. (CANopenEditor lists EDS, XDD v1.0/1.1, CANopenNode V4 and Markdown exporters. Confirm the CLI flag names against the pinned release.) The drift gate is odgen --check in CI. It regenerates every artefact and fails if any checked-in file differs, or if 0x1018:03 revision / OD hash (0x5FFE) was not bumped when the dictionary changed. 4.3 Transport abstraction ¶ All CANopen semantics live in one CANopenNode instance. Transports are ports under one CO_CANmodule . flowchart TB subgraph stack["CANopenNode CO_t (one OD)"] SDO1["SDO server 1 (0x600/0x580+id)"] SDO2["SDO server 2 (wireless channel)"] PDO["RPDO/TPDO, SYNC, EMCY, HB, NMT, LSS"] end COD2["CO_driver_hardfoc.c
(CO_CANsend, rx dispatch, error status)"] R["FrameRouter
per-port RX allow-list, TX fan-out, rate limit"] P0["Port 0: EspTwaiPort (classic)
later StmFdcanPort (FD)"] P1["Port 1: TunnelPort Wi-Fi TLS"] P2["Port 2: TunnelPort ESP-NOW"] P3["Host: LinuxSocketCanPort / PipePort"] stack <--> COD2 <--> R R <--> P0 R <--> P1 R <--> P2 R <--> P3 contracts/can_frame.hpp : struct CanFrame { // transport-neutral; FD-sized from day one uint32_t id ; // 11- or 29-bit uint8_t len ; // 0..8 classic, 0..64 FD (bytes, not DLC code) uint8_t flags ; // EXT | RTR | FDF | BRS | ESI uint8_t data [ 64 ]; uint32_t ts_us ; // RX timestamp (ISR-captured) }; struct PortCaps { bool fd ; uint8_t max_len ; uint32_t nominal_bps , data_bps ; uint8_t hw_filters ; }; class ICanPort { // implemented per binding; Send is non-blocking public : virtual PortCaps Caps () const = 0 ; virtual TxResult Send ( const CanFrame & ) = 0 ; // Ok | QueueFull | BusOff | NotAllowed virtual void SetRxSink ( void ( * sink )( void * , const CanFrame & ), void * ctx ) = 0 ; // ISR-safe sink virtual PortStatus Status () const = 0 ; // TEC/REC, state, overruns virtual bool Recover () = 0 ; // bus-off recovery request }; Router policy, as a table in contracts: Port RX accepted TX sent Notes CAN (0) everything except SDO-server-2 COB-IDs (dropped, so a CAN node cannot pose as the wireless client) everything except SDO-server-2 responses normal CANopen Wi-Fi / ESP-NOW tunnel SDO-server-2 requests. NMT and RPDO only if 0x2701 authority policy allows SDO-server-2 responses, plus subscribed mirrors of HB, EMCY and selected TPDOs (rate-limited per port, default ≤ 100 Hz each) read-mostly by default Host sim (P3) as CAN as CAN CI SDO server 2 (0x1201) is predefined with virtual COB-IDs (client→server 0x6C0+id, server→client 0x5C0+id, documented as tunnel-only). These IDs never appear on the physical bus. For human or script access, the CiA 309-3 gateway ( CO_gateway_ascii.c ) uses CANopenNode's local SDO client ( CO_CONFIG_SDO_CLI_LOCAL , 301/CO_config.h:401 ), so ASCII commands for the node's own ID access the OD without bus traffic. Together this gives identical SDO semantics everywhere: the same abort codes, the same OD extension handlers and the same access checks. The C++ side has no 8-byte assumptions. CO_CANrxMsg_t and CO_CANtx_t in the new CO_driver_target.h carry data[CO_CAN_MAX_LEN] , which is 8 on classic builds and 64 on FD builds. The router rejects any frame longer than the destination port's Caps().max_len , and the PDO layer checks mapped length against CO_PDO_MAX_SIZE (§8). 4.4 Threads, priorities and timing on the single-core C6 ¶ Platform facts: ESP32-C6, one HP RISC-V core at 160 MHz ( CONFIG_ESP_DEFAULT_CPU_FREQ_MHZ=160 ). ESP-IDF built-in priorities are Wi-Fi 23, esp_timer 22, event loop 20 and lwIP 18. Espressif reserves 24 for very short timing-critical bursts and advises that network-using tasks run below 18 ( IDF speed guide ). Prerequisite: CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 (set; bench soak still needed). Thread / context Prio Trigger / period Owns Budget Liveness TWAI ISR ISR RX/TX/error none (copies to lock-free ring, timestamps, Wake(drive_rt) on SYNC/RPDO COB-IDs, Wake(co_svc) on others) < 5 µs/frame n/a gptimer ISR ISR free-run tick when no SYNC is configured (default 1 ms) none < 2 µs n/a drive_rt 24 SYNC (or gptimer) event; 2 ms backstop SPI2 (TMC9660, AS5047U), CiA 402 FSM, RPDO/TPDO processing WCET ≤ 300 µs at 1 kHz (step aborted to safe stop if > 1 ms) critical, 5 ms safety 21 5 ms fixed rate LivenessMonitor , SafetyArbiter , task-WDT feed ≤ 50 µs n/a (it is the monitor; TWDT watches it) i2c_io 19 PCAL INT (GPIO23) events + 10 ms backstop I2C (PCAL95555: DRV_EN, faults, CAN STB; BNO08x) blocking I/O, preemptible critical, 100 ms co_svc 17 CAN RX wake + 1 ms timer-next (CANopenNode timerNext_us ) CO_process (NMT, HB producer/consumer, EMCY, SDO servers incl. block, LSS, TIME), OD extensions, storage requests ≤ 200 µs typical critical, 50 ms wl_gw 15 socket / ESP-NOW queue TLS tunnel, ESP-NOW peer table, optional 309-3 — non-critical housekeep 6 100 ms fault-journal flush (only when motion is not enabled), LED, diagnostics, NVS writes — non-critical, 1 s app_main supervisor 1 1 s boot orchestration ( VortexSystemThread init table) — — Notes: drive_rt at 24 is short by construction. The TMC9660 runs the fast loops (PWM-rate current loop and internal velocity/position loops), so each cycle is about six TMCL SPI exchanges plus one AS5047U read. Commissioning and bulk configuration (hundreds of TMCL writes) go through a bounded service slot in the same thread: at most N transactions per cycle, default 2. The bus therefore keeps a single owner, and RT jitter stays bounded. This is the RunInBackground lesson from the pw threading model, applied to a single core. Blocking chip bring-up (TMC bootloader, BNO08x reset) runs at boot before drive_rt starts, or in the service slot. It never runs inline at priority 24. safety sits below Wi-Fi and esp_timer. Its 5 ms deadline tolerates Wi-Fi bursts. The fast reactions do not depend on it: drive_rt enforces limits and stops on TMC fault flags in the same cycle, and the TMC9660 SPI heartbeat (§5.5) stops the motor if drive_rt itself stalls. Flash writes (NVS) stall cache-resident code on the C6. Storage is therefore refused while the drive is in Operation Enabled : 0x1010 returns SDO abort 0x08000022 , and journal writes are buffered in RAM (§6). drive_rt cycle (cyclic synchronous modes): sequenceDiagram participant M as Master (PC/PLC) participant ISR as TWAI ISR participant RT as drive_rt (24) participant TMC as TMC9660 (SPI2) M->>ISR: RPDO (target) then SYNC ISR->>RT: Wake (SYNC timestamp t0) RT->>RT: drain RX ring, CO_process_SYNC, CO_process_RPDO RT->>RT: Cia402 step (rule table), limits, mode logic RT->>TMC: SAP target (pos/vel/torque) + GAP status/actuals (about 6 TMCL) RT->>RT: AS5047U read (1 frame), publish seqlock snapshot RT->>ISR: CO_process_TPDO (sync TPDOs queued, non-blocking) ISR->>M: TPDOs (actual values from cycle n-1 consistent set) RT->>RT: live::Beat(drive_rt), record step time 4.5 Timing budget at 1 Mbit/s ¶ Classic base-format data frame with n data bytes: 47 + 8 n bits nominal (including 3-bit IFS). Worst-case bit stuffing adds ⌊(34 + 8 n − 1)/4⌋ bits. At 1 Mbit/s an 8-byte frame takes 111 µs nominal and 135 µs worst case. SYNC (0 bytes) takes 47–55 µs. Default CSP traffic per node per cycle: RPDO2 (controlword + target position, 6 B, ≤ 115 µs), TPDO2 (statusword + position actual, 6 B, ≤ 115 µs) and TPDO3 (statusword + velocity actual, 6 B, ≤ 115 µs). About 345 µs per node, plus a shared SYNC of 55 µs. CPU estimate per 1 kHz cycle on the C6: RX drain about 20 µs, SYNC/RPDO/TPDO processing about 40 µs, FSM and limits about 10 µs, six TMCL exchanges at 10 MHz SPI about 150 µs (to be measured, about 25 µs each in polling mode), AS5047U about 15 µs. That is roughly 235 µs, or 24 % CPU. The TMC9660 samples targets in a ~1 kHz internal loop that is not phase-locked to SYNC (Erratum 4 note, vortex_bench_safety.hpp:169 ), so expect up to 1 ms of extra transport delay. 1 kHz is the ceiling. 250–500 Hz is the recommended default for csp/csv/cst. 0x60C2 (interpolation time period) mirrors 0x1006, and drive_rt linearly interpolates targets when the SYNC period exceeds 1 ms. 5. This applies when 0x2701:03 "require master liveness" = 1 (the default). The deadman therefore always exists. Loss of any configured liveness source triggers the 0x6007 reaction: default 1 = Fault, which applies 0x605E. 0x1029:01 drives the NMT reaction. CANopenNode raises its own EMCYs (heartbeat consumer timeout, SYNC timeout, RPDO timeout) through CO_EM . The node translates them into FaultBook causes, so the 402 reaction and the journal entry come from the same table. Additionally, the TMC9660 SPI heartbeat monitor is enabled ( HEARTBEAT_MONITORING_CONFIG = SPI , timeout 20 ms; tmc9660_param_mode_tmcl.hpp:460 ). drive_rt exchanges with the chip at least every cycle, and at ≥ 100 Hz when idle. If the ESP32 hangs, crashes or is held in reset, the TMC9660 stops the bridge on its own ( HEARTBEAT_STOPPED flag) with the configured stop behaviour. That is the independent hardware path. 5.6 CiA 402 state machine as a rule table ¶ stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> NotReadyToSwitchOn NotReadyToSwitchOn --> SwitchOnDisabled: 1 (self-test ok) SwitchOnDisabled --> ReadyToSwitchOn: 2 shutdown ReadyToSwitchOn --> SwitchedOn: 3 switch on (config applied, limits valid) SwitchedOn --> OperationEnabled: 4 enable op (liveness gate, authority gate) OperationEnabled --> SwitchedOn: 5 disable op (0x605C) SwitchedOn --> ReadyToSwitchOn: 6 shutdown ReadyToSwitchOn --> SwitchOnDisabled: 7 quick stop / disable voltage OperationEnabled --> ReadyToSwitchOn: 8 shutdown (0x605B) OperationEnabled --> SwitchOnDisabled: 9 disable voltage SwitchedOn --> SwitchOnDisabled: 10 OperationEnabled --> QuickStopActive: 11 quick stop (0x605A) QuickStopActive --> SwitchOnDisabled: 12 stop done / disable voltage QuickStopActive --> OperationEnabled: 16 enable op (only option codes 5..8) OperationEnabled --> FaultReactionActive: 13 fault SwitchedOn --> FaultReactionActive: 13 ReadyToSwitchOn --> FaultReactionActive: 13 FaultReactionActive --> Fault: 14 reaction done (0x605E) Fault --> SwitchOnDisabled: 15 fault reset (cw bit7 rising, cause cleared) contracts/cia402_rules.hpp implements constexpr Decision Decide(State, ControlwordCmd, Inputs) . It follows the pattern of pw_shared/system/clinical_lifecycle.hpp:166 : a single documented table, pure and host-tested. Controlword decode uses CiA 402 masks (shutdown xxxx x110 , switch on 0111 , enable 1111 , disable voltage xx0x , quick stop x01x , fault reset bit 7 edge). Statusword encode covers bits 0–6 per state, bit 7 warning, bit 9 remote (set when the controlword source holds authority), bit 10 target reached, bit 11 internal limit active and bits 12/13 per mode (pp: set-point ack / following error; hm: attained / error; csp/csv/cst: target ignored / following error). Transition 3 is where the OD application parameters are validated and pushed to the TMC9660, in the service slot. Transition 4 sets the commutation mode and asserts DRV_EN . Transitions out of Operation Enabled first set the TMC target to zero or ramp per the option code, and then switch commutation to SYSTEM_OFF or SYSTEM_OFF_LOW_SIDE_FETS_ON as the option code requires. 6. Motor-agnostic drive, faults and persistence ¶ 6.1 Motor and feedback catalog ¶ The approach follows pw-controller-sw/docs/software/bldc-motor-catalog.md : numbers live in one header of catalog rows. A SKU swap means picking a row id or uploading a custom row, never hunting through code. hal/.../config/VortexMotorCatalog.hpp holds constexpr rows: id, slug, tmcl::MotorType , pole pairs, rated/peak mA, Rs, Ls, Kt, max rpm, PWM Hz, default commutation, Hall/ABN data, safe tuning seeds. Row 0 is none . Row 1 is bench_24v_30w_bldc , seeded from vortex_bench_safety.hpp : 7 pole pairs, 390 µH, 25 kHz, 2.5 A max phase, I²t 2.5 A/2 s and 2.0 A/5 s. Further rows: generic_nema17_stepper , generic_brushed_dc , custom (all values from 0x3001–0x3008). 0x3000 selects a row. Selecting copies the row into 0x3001–0x3008 (application group), and the user may then edit. The OD stays the truth: the TMC9660's own NVM ( NvmStorage ) is not used. The chip is re-programmed from the OD at every transition 3. Feedback choices map to the TMC enums. Commutation: open-loop voltage/current, ABN, Hall, SPI encoder. Velocity and position sensors: same-as-commutation, Hall, ABN1, ABN2, SPI. The host AS5047U can serve as (a) an alignment and verification reference during commissioning, (b) an output-shaft absolute position in 0x60E4 (with 0x3009 gear ratio) for homing method 35/37 seeding, and © a plausibility monitor (commutation encoder vs. host encoder divergence → EMCY 0x7300-class). It cannot close the TMC loop unless the board routes it to the TMC SPI-encoder or ABI pins (Q5). The Hall/ABN bootloader mux ( BootloaderConfig ) depends on the board. It is a build-time board fact, held in the catalog's board section, not an OD object. Changing 0x3003 to a feedback whose pins are not muxed is rejected with SDO abort 0x06090030 (value range) and a hint code in 0x3021. 6.2 Safe defaults and limit enforcement ¶ With factory defaults, row 0 ( none ) refuses transition 3 with EMCY 0x6320 ("parameter error") until a row is selected and stored. Limits clamp in three layers, and the effective value is the minimum: board limit (compile-time: shunt, MOSFET, connector rating) ≥ catalog row peak ≥ 0x6073/0x6072/0x60E0/0x60E1. Writes beyond the board limit abort with 0x06090031 (value too high). TMC protection (OV/UV, OT, OC, I²t) is always programmed from 0x3007 before DRV_EN . Torque mode (tq/cst) needs an explicit 0x6080 max motor speed. It feeds the ESP task watchdog only while the critical verdict is clean. Only safety subscribes to the TWDT, with the timeout reduced from 5 s to 500 ms. On a critical stall it commands, in order: TMC SYSTEM_OFF (if drive_rt is not the stalled thread), then DRV_EN low via i2c_io , then a journal entry, then it stops feeding the watchdog. Independent path: the TMC9660 SPI heartbeat (§5.5) and the hardware DRV_EN pull-down (verify on the schematic, Q6). 6.6 Service-only objects ¶ 0x4100 (raw TMCL bridge), the commissioning commands and 0x2601 secrets are gated twice. The writer must hold authority, and the node must be in Pre-operational or Switched On (never Operation Enabled). 6.7 Persistence ¶ Groups and keys: od_comm (0x1010:02), od_app (0x1010:03), od_cal (0x1010:04) in namespace vortex_cfg ; lss (node-ID, bit-rate index) in vortex_cfg ; secrets in vortex under a separate key; the fault journal ring in a new namespace vortex_log . The NVS partition should be encrypted ( nvs_flash_secure_init + flash encryption) if secrets are stored (Q8). Record format, versioned by OD address rather than memory layout. Header {magic VXOD , u16 format, u32 OD hash, u32 count, u32 crc32}, followed by TLV records {u16 index, u8 sub, u8 type, u8 len, value}. On restore, every record whose (index, sub, type) exists in the current OD with persist = its group is range-checked and applied. Unknown or invalid records are dropped and counted (0x2800). Missing ones keep defaults. Changing the OD therefore never bricks a stored configuration. A YAML migrations: list can map renamed addresses. CANopenNode integration: CO_storage_init with custom store / restore callbacks that serialise the TLV list for each entry group. This replaces CO_storageBlank.c . 0x1011 writes a "restore pending" flag, and defaults apply after the next reset (CiA 301 semantics). Store is refused in Operation Enabled (flash cache stall, §4.4) with abort 0x08000022 , and it runs in co_svc . LSS: CANopenNode's LSS slave store callback ( CO_LSSslave_initCfgStoreCallback ) writes lss . At boot the order is LSS-stored node-ID → Kconfig default → 0xFF (unconfigured, LSS only). The bit-rate index follows the CiA 305 table (0 = 1 M, 1 = 800 k, 2 = 500 k, 3 = 250 k, 4 = 125 k, 6 = 50 k, 7 = 20 k, 8 = 10 k). The CommChannelsManager hard-coded 500 kbit/s becomes the value read from lss , applied before EspCan init. "Activate bit timing" re-initialises the TWAI node after the switch delay. 7. Wireless paths ¶ 7.1 Recommendation ¶ Path Recommendation Why Wi-Fi STA + TLS tunnel (binary frame records) Primary wireless path (Phase 2) python-canopen works unchanged through a python-can bus plugin ( interface="vortex" , channel="tls://host:port" ), so the whole CLI and test suite runs over Wi-Fi. Throughput is high, and it is reachable from any PC on the LAN CiA 309-3 ASCII over TLS-TCP Optional (Phase 3) Human- and script-friendly (" [1] 5 r 0x6041 0 u16 "). CANopenNode ships CO_gateway_ascii.c and can address the whole CAN bus as a gateway. It is valuable for integrators and needs no special client ESP-NOW Secondary (Phase 3): a PC dongle (any ESP32-C6/S3 board running vortex-espnow-bridge firmware exposing slcan over USB-CDC), plus board-to-board links No AP is needed and latency is low. slcan is supported by python-can on all OSes, so the dongle looks like a USB-CAN adapter. The same frame-record codec is used BLE Commissioning only, if wanted (Q4): IDF network provisioning (security 2, SRP6a) to set Wi-Fi credentials Avoids typing secrets into SDO from a PC 7.2 Frame-record tunnel (shared by Wi-Fi and ESP-NOW) ¶ Datagram format: {u8 ver=1, u8 flags, u16 seq, u32 ack/epoch, then records: {u32 id|EXT|RTR, u8 flags FDF/BRS/ESI, u8 len, data[len]}...} . A record is the transport form of CanFrame , so FD lengths are already representable. Wi-Fi carries the stream over TLS 1.3 PSK (mbedTLS via esp-tls). ESP-NOW carries one datagram per action frame: ≤ 250 B for v1 compatibility, ≤ 1470 B with v2. That is up to 23 classic frames per v1 datagram. Records arrive at the router as from any other port (§4.3), with that port's policy. 7.3 Security ¶ ESP-NOW: unicast only, CCMP-encrypted with a per-peer LMK under a device PMK. Broadcast or multicast cannot be encrypted, so the node ignores broadcast data except a signed pairing beacon. At most 17 encrypted peers; the IDF default is 7 ( CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_ESPNOW_MAX_ENCRYPT_NUM ). Keys are set over CAN or USB (0x2601, write-only) or by a pairing button sequence. An application sequence number with a replay window is added on top of CCMP. Wi-Fi: credentials are provisioned via 0x2601 or BLE provisioning. The TLS-PSK identity and key are per device. There is no plaintext listener. Auth failures are rate-limited and counted in 0x2602. mDNS advertises _vortex-co._tcp for discovery. NVS encryption is required whenever secrets are present (Q8). 7.4 Safety rules (never bypass) ¶ By default 0x2701 allows enable (transition 4) from CAN only. A wireless writer of 0x6040 is accepted only for transitions towards safety (disable operation, disable voltage, quick stop). Shutdown/switch-on/enable (transitions ⅔/4) and fault reset are rejected with abort 0x08000022 . If a user sets 0x2701 to allow wireless enable, the wireless port must hold authority (0x2700 request/grant). It must send a deadman (tunnel keep-alive or HB mirror) at least every 0x2701:02 ms (default 200). On loss, the 0x6007 reaction applies. Authority changes only in Switched On or below. A request from another transport while one holds authority is refused. The CAN master can always revoke authority, because CAN wins. NMT from wireless is limited by default to Reset Node / Pre-operational (Stop and Start need policy). Wireless never writes 0x1010, 0x4100 or 0x2601 unless policy bit "wireless service" is set. 7.5 Expectations (to be measured on the bench) ¶ Path One-way latency (typ.) CAN FD readiness ¶ What is abstracted now: CanFrame with len ≤ 64 plus FDF/BRS/ESI. PortCaps reports fd and max_len . The router enforces the per-port length. BaseCan v2 in hf-internal-interface-wrap gets an FD-sized message ( data[64] , byte length, flags). The FD flags stay on the current hf_can_message_t only after data is enlarged. Until then SetDLC > 8 must be rejected, which fixes the latent overrun (§3). CO_driver_target.h uses CO_CAN_MAX_LEN . Stack config CO_PDO_MAX_SIZE comes from one place. YAML mapping limits are per build ( fd_only objects are compiled out on classic). The PDO profile tables in contracts declare classic and FD variants. CiA 402-6 defines CANopen FD PDO mapping, and the FD variants follow it. On FD, one RPDO (controlword + target + offsets) and one TPDO (status + all actuals + error + temperatures, about 24 B) replace RPDO2–4 and TPDO2–4. At 1 / 5 Mbit/s this is about 70 µs per frame instead of 2–3 × 135 µs. What an STM32 FDCAN binding needs: StmFdcanPort : ICanPort with nominal and data bit timing, TDC ( SetTransmitterDelayCompensation , already in BaseCan ), RX FIFO interrupt → sink, TX FIFO non-blocking, bus-off auto-recovery policy, and hardware filter banks (FDCAN has many, so useCANrxFilters = true ). Stack: CANopenNode v4 has no CiA 1301. Its PDO path assumes ≤ 8 bytes in at least one place: bitwise-mapping copies CO_PDO_MAX_SIZE bytes into a uint64_t ( 301/CO_PDO.c:787-789 ). Mapping entries are limited to 8. Two options, decided when hardware exists (Q9): (a) Extend CANopenNode: 64-byte PDOs with bitwise mapping disabled, more mapping entries, an FD EMCY format and a new USDO server module. Upstream the work. (b) Replace the stack behind CoStack with a commercial CiA 1301 stack (for example emotas or MicroControl, which advertise CiA 1301). Either way the OD YAML, contracts, drive app, router and tools are unchanged. The generator gains an XDD (CiA 1311) emitter, and python tooling needs a USDO client. python-canopen has none today, so it would be a small added module. USDO uses the 0x600/0x580+id ranges with destination addressing in the payload, and it is not backward compatible with CiA 301 SDO. CiA 1301 is a separate network mode, not a per-frame option. A node runs either CANopen CC or CANopen FD on a given bus. The Kconfig/CMake option VORTEX_CANOPEN_FD selects the stack mode, and the YAML marks SDO vs USDO channel objects. 9. docs.title: Vortex V1 CANopen Device: Design

docs.text: Vortex V1 should become a CiA 402 servo drive node on its CAN port. It should keep one object dictionary (OD), described in a single YAML source. That source generates the CANopenNode OD.c/OD.h , the CiA 306 EDS file, C++ index constants and the Python constants. Every transport carries the same CANopen services against that OD: the TWAI port today, a CAN FD port on a future STM32, ESP-NOW and Wi-Fi. Motion is driven by the TMC9660's own current, velocity, position and ramp loops. The ESP32-C6 runs the CiA 402 state machine, mode logic, limits, the fault arbiter and the communication stack. The repository already has the pieces (CANopenNode v4 as a submodule, a CO_driver shim, managers for every chip), but the current CAN path does not work on hardware (§3). The plan therefore rebuilds the integration rather than extending it. Key decisions: Stack: CANopenNode v4 (Apache-2.0, already vendored) behind a narrow CoStack seam, so a CiA 1301 stack can replace it later without touching application code. Single source of truth: od/vortex_od.yaml generates firmware, EDS, documentation and Python. CI fails on drift. Transport router: one CO_CANmodule that fans out to N ICanPort bindings, with per-port COB-ID policy. Wireless gets its own SDO server channel and read-only mirrors. It never gets motion authority by default. Threads: one SYNC-driven real-time owner thread for SPI2 (TMC9660 + AS5047U). It runs as a short burst at the highest priority. A separate service thread handles SDO, storage and NMT. An I2C owner thread handles the PCAL95555 and BNO08x. A safety monitor gates the task watchdog. The TMC9660's own SPI heartbeat is the independent last-resort stop. Wireless: Wi-Fi with a TLS tunnel that python-can can use as a bus, so the same tools work over Wi-Fi as over USB-CAN. CiA 309-3 ASCII is an optional extra. ESP-NOW is for a USB dongle that bridges to a PC (slcan). It also serves board-to-board links. Verification: the same node application and OD build for Linux and run against vcan0 , or against a pipe bus where vcan is unavailable. They are exercised by pytest and python-canopen against a simulated motor.
docs.title: 1. Summary

docs.text: G1: A complete, conformant-in-spirit CANopen device on the board's CAN port: CiA 301 NMT, heartbeat, SYNC, TIME, EMCY, SDO (expedited, segmented, block), PDO with runtime mapping, 0x1010/0x1011 store/restore, identity, and CiA 305 LSS. G2: Easy to exercise with a USB-CAN adapter on Windows, Linux or macOS, using a single pip install tool. G3: Motor-agnostic. BLDC/PMSM, stepper and brushed DC, with Hall, ABN, SPI-encoder or open-loop feedback, are selected and commissioned through OD objects. No rebuild is needed. G4: Expose the IMU (BNO08x), the absolute encoder (AS5047U), temperatures, power rails, spare GPIO, expansion slots and the LED. G5: Extra access paths over Wi-Fi and ESP-NOW that use the same OD semantics and never weaken safety. G6: CAN FD on a future STM32 should be a port-binding and stack-configuration change, not an application rewrite.
docs.title: 2.1 Goals

docs.text: CiA 402-4 functional safety (STO/SS1 certification). The design is safety-aware, but nothing in it is safety-rated. Firmware update over CANopen (CiA 302-3, 0x1F50/0x1F51). The partition layout is prepared for it (§10, step 12). The protocol is deferred. Acting as an NMT master or CiA 402 master for other drives. This is what the current CANOpenBLDCThread does, and it is removed (§10). CANopen safety (SRDO, CiA 304), CiA 302 network management, and Thread/Zigbee on 802.15.4. CiA conformance certification. Conformance- style tests are in scope. Certification needs a CiA vendor ID and a test house (open question Q1).

docs.title: 3. What exists today (verified)

docs.text:
The layout follows pw-controller-sw/firmware/README.md . A header-only contracts package holds the shared types and pure rule tables. The HAL owns hardware, the app owns threads, and host tests link only contracts and the app logic. flowchart TB subgraph tools["Host tools (PC)"] CLI["vortex-canopen CLI
(python-canopen + python-can)"] EDS["vortex_v1.eds (generated)"] end subgraph app["hardfoc-vortex-v1 / main (node app)"] NODE["CoNode: CANopenNode instance,
OD extensions, storage, LSS"] DRV["DriveAxis: CiA 402 FSM, modes,
limits, commissioning"] SAF["SafetyArbiter + LivenessMonitor"] WL["Wireless: WiFi tunnel, ESP-NOW, 309-3 (opt)"] ROUTE["FrameRouter (N ports, COB-ID policy)"] end subgraph contracts["hardfoc-vortex-v1 / contracts (header-only, host-tested)"] ODT["Generated OD ids + record types"] FSM["Cia402 rule table, fault policy table,
authority rules, PDO profile tables"] FR["CanFrame (len<=64, FDF/BRS/ESI), port caps"] end subgraph hal["hf-hal-vortex-v1 (board HAL facades)"] AX["AxisPort facade (TMC9660 via MotorController)"] SENS["Encoder / IMU / Temp / Gpio / Led facades"] NVS["NvsManager"] CANP["CAN port binding (EspTwaiPort)"] end subgraph core["hf-core"] BASE["BaseCan v2, BaseSpi, BaseI2c, EspCan/StmCan"] H["Tmc9660Handler, As5047uHandler,
Bno08xHandler, Pcal95555Handler"] COD["CO_driver_hardfoc.c (generic over ICanPort)"] end CLI --> EDS NODE --> ODT DRV --> FSM SAF --> FSM ROUTE --> FR NODE --> ROUTE ROUTE --> CANP WL --> ROUTE DRV --> AX NODE --> SENS NODE --> NVS AX --> H SENS --> H CANP --> BASE NODE --> COD COD --> FR Rules (adapted from pw-hal/README.md "Design rules"): The node app never includes twai.h , EspCan.h or chip drivers. It uses HAL facades ( AxisPort , ImuFacade , …) and the ICanPort interface. Contracts contain no .cpp , no RTOS and no HAL. They hold the CiA 402 transition table, fault policy table, authority rules, PDO profile tables and generated OD identifiers. Host tests use them directly. One bus has one owner thread (see pw-controller-sw/docs/software/threading-model.md §4): SPI2 belongs to drive_rt , and I2C belongs to i2c_io . Hot paths bind once at init. They do no string lookups ( GpioManager::Get(std::string_view) ) per cycle.
