docs.text:
flowchart LR Y["od/vortex_od.yaml
(objects, types, access, PDO-mappable,
defaults, limits, units, persist group,
FD max lengths, docs)"] --> G["tools/odgen (Python)"] G --> ODC["OD.c / OD.h
(CANopenNode v4 format)"] G --> EDSF["vortex_v1.eds (CiA 306)"] G --> HPP["contracts/vortex_od_ids.hpp
+ record structs"] G --> PY["vortex_canopen/od_ids.py
+ packaged EDS"] G --> MD["docs/od-reference.md"] G --> XDD["vortex_v1.xdd (CiA 1311, later for FD)"] ODC --> FW["firmware build"] EDSF --> CLI2["python-canopen import_od"] The YAML schema mirrors the CiA 306 attributes: ParameterName , ObjectType , DataType , AccessType , PDOMapping , DefaultValue , LowLimit / HighLimit . It adds: persist: comm|app|cal|none , od_extension: <C++ handler> (dynamic objects served from snapshots), fd_only: bool and units . odgen writes OD.c/OD.h in the exact CANopenNode v4 layout. A CI job cross-checks the output by importing the generated EDS with the pinned CANopenEditor EDSSharp CLI, exporting "CANopenNode V4", and diffing the structural content (entries, sub-counts, attributes). The in-house emitter is primary because it runs anywhere without .NET. CANopenEditor is the independent oracle. (CANopenEditor lists EDS, XDD v1.0/1.1, CANopenNode V4 and Markdown exporters. Confirm the CLI flag names against the pinned release.) The drift gate is odgen --check in CI. It regenerates every artefact and fails if any checked-in file differs, or if 0x1018:03 revision / OD hash (0x5FFE) was not bumped when the dictionary changed.
docs.title: 4.2 Object dictionary as the single source of truth

docs.text:
All CANopen semantics live in one CANopenNode instance. Transports are ports under one CO_CANmodule . flowchart TB subgraph stack["CANopenNode CO_t (one OD)"] SDO1["SDO server 1 (0x600/0x580+id)"] SDO2["SDO server 2 (wireless channel)"] PDO["RPDO/TPDO, SYNC, EMCY, HB, NMT, LSS"] end COD2["CO_driver_hardfoc.c
(CO_CANsend, rx dispatch, error status)"] R["FrameRouter
per-port RX allow-list, TX fan-out, rate limit"] P0["Port 0: EspTwaiPort (classic)
later StmFdcanPort (FD)"] P1["Port 1: TunnelPort Wi-Fi TLS"] P2["Port 2: TunnelPort ESP-NOW"] P3["Host: LinuxSocketCanPort / PipePort"] stack <--> COD2 <--> R R <--> P0 R <--> P1 R <--> P2 R <--> P3 contracts/can_frame.hpp : struct CanFrame { // transport-neutral; FD-sized from day one uint32_t id ; // 11- or 29-bit uint8_t len ; // 0..8 classic, 0..64 FD (bytes, not DLC code) uint8_t flags ; // EXT | RTR | FDF | BRS | ESI uint8_t data [ 64 ]; uint32_t ts_us ; // RX timestamp (ISR-captured) }; struct PortCaps { bool fd ; uint8_t max_len ; uint32_t nominal_bps , data_bps ; uint8_t hw_filters ; }; class ICanPort { // implemented per binding; Send is non-blocking public : virtual PortCaps Caps () const = 0 ; virtual TxResult Send ( const CanFrame & ) = 0 ; // Ok | QueueFull | BusOff | NotAllowed virtual void SetRxSink ( void ( * sink )( void * , const CanFrame & ), void * ctx ) = 0 ; // ISR-safe sink virtual PortStatus Status () const = 0 ; // TEC/REC, state, overruns virtual bool Recover () = 0 ; // bus-off recovery request }; Router policy, as a table in contracts: Port RX accepted TX sent Notes CAN (0) everything except SDO-server-2 COB-IDs (dropped, so a CAN node cannot pose as the wireless client) everything except SDO-server-2 responses normal CANopen Wi-Fi / ESP-NOW tunnel SDO-server-2 requests. NMT and RPDO only if 0x2701 authority policy allows SDO-server-2 responses, plus subscribed mirrors of HB, EMCY and selected TPDOs (rate-limited per port, default ≤ 100 Hz each) read-mostly by default Host sim (P3) as CAN as CAN CI SDO server 2 (0x1201) is predefined with virtual COB-IDs (client→server 0x6C0+id, server→client 0x5C0+id, documented as tunnel-only). These IDs never appear on the physical bus. For human or script access, the CiA 309-3 gateway ( CO_gateway_ascii.c ) uses CANopenNode's local SDO client ( CO_CONFIG_SDO_CLI_LOCAL , 301/CO_config.h:401 ), so ASCII commands for the node's own ID access the OD without bus traffic. Together this gives identical SDO semantics everywhere: the same abort codes, the same OD extension handlers and the same access checks. The C++ side has no 8-byte assumptions. CO_CANrxMsg_t and CO_CANtx_t in the new CO_driver_target.h carry data[CO_CAN_MAX_LEN] , which is 8 on classic builds and 64 on FD builds. The router rejects any frame longer than the destination port's Caps().max_len , and the PDO layer checks mapped length against CO_PDO_MAX_SIZE (§8).
docs.title: 4.3 Transport abstraction

docs.text: Platform facts: ESP32-C6, one HP RISC-V core at 160 MHz ( CONFIG_ESP_DEFAULT_CPU_FREQ_MHZ=160 ). ESP-IDF built-in priorities are Wi-Fi 23, esp_timer 22, event loop 20 and lwIP 18. Espressif reserves 24 for very short timing-critical bursts and advises that network-using tasks run below 18 ( IDF speed guide ). Prerequisite: CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 (set; bench soak still needed). Thread / context Prio Trigger / period Owns Budget Liveness TWAI ISR ISR RX/TX/error none (copies to lock-free ring, timestamps, Wake(drive_rt) on SYNC/RPDO COB-IDs, Wake(co_svc) on others) < 5 µs/frame n/a gptimer ISR ISR free-run tick when no SYNC is configured (default 1 ms) none < 2 µs n/a drive_rt 24 SYNC (or gptimer) event; 2 ms backstop SPI2 (TMC9660, AS5047U), CiA 402 FSM, RPDO/TPDO processing WCET ≤ 300 µs at 1 kHz (step aborted to safe stop if > 1 ms) critical, 5 ms safety 21 5 ms fixed rate LivenessMonitor , SafetyArbiter , task-WDT feed ≤ 50 µs n/a (it is the monitor; TWDT watches it) i2c_io 19 PCAL INT (GPIO23) events + 10 ms backstop I2C (PCAL95555: DRV_EN, faults, CAN STB; BNO08x) blocking I/O, preemptible critical, 100 ms co_svc 17 CAN RX wake + 1 ms timer-next (CANopenNode timerNext_us ) CO_process (NMT, HB producer/consumer, EMCY, SDO servers incl. block, LSS, TIME), OD extensions, storage requests ≤ 200 µs typical critical, 50 ms wl_gw 15 socket / ESP-NOW queue TLS tunnel, ESP-NOW peer table, optional 309-3 — non-critical housekeep 6 100 ms fault-journal flush (only when motion is not enabled), LED, diagnostics, NVS writes — non-critical, 1 s app_main supervisor 1 1 s boot orchestration ( VortexSystemThread init table) — — Notes: drive_rt at 24 is short by construction. The TMC9660 runs the fast loops (PWM-rate current loop and internal velocity/position loops), so each cycle is about six TMCL SPI exchanges plus one AS5047U read. Commissioning and bulk configuration (hundreds of TMCL writes) go through a bounded service slot in the same thread: at most N transactions per cycle, default 2. The bus therefore keeps a single owner, and RT jitter stays bounded. This is the RunInBackground lesson from the pw threading model, applied to a single core. Blocking chip bring-up (TMC bootloader, BNO08x reset) runs at boot before drive_rt starts, or in the service slot. It never runs inline at priority 24. safety sits below Wi-Fi and esp_timer. Its 5 ms deadline tolerates Wi-Fi bursts. The fast reactions do not depend on it: drive_rt enforces limits and stops on TMC fault flags in the same cycle, and the TMC9660 SPI heartbeat (§5.5) stops the motor if drive_rt itself stalls. Flash writes (NVS) stall cache-resident code on the C6. Storage is therefore refused while the drive is in Operation Enabled : 0x1010 returns SDO abort 0x08000022 , and journal writes are buffered in RAM (§6). drive_rt cycle (cyclic synchronous modes): sequenceDiagram participant M as Master (PC/PLC) participant ISR as TWAI ISR participant RT as drive_rt (24) participant TMC as TMC9660 (SPI2) M->>ISR: RPDO (target) then SYNC ISR->>RT: Wake (SYNC timestamp t0) RT->>RT: drain RX ring, CO_process_SYNC, CO_process_RPDO RT->>RT: Cia402 step (rule table), limits, mode logic RT->>TMC: SAP target (pos/vel/torque) + GAP status/actuals (about 6 TMCL) RT->>RT: AS5047U read (1 frame), publish seqlock snapshot RT->>ISR: CO_process_TPDO (sync TPDOs queued, non-blocking) ISR->>M: TPDOs (actual values from cycle n-1 consistent set) RT->>RT: live::Beat(drive_rt), record step time
docs.title: 4.4 Threads, priorities and timing on the single-core C6

docs.text: Classic base-format data frame with n data bytes: 47 + 8 n bits nominal (including 3-bit IFS). Worst-case bit stuffing adds ⌊(34 + 8 n − 1)/4⌋ bits. At 1 Mbit/s an 8-byte frame takes 111 µs nominal and 135 µs worst case. SYNC (0 bytes) takes 47–55 µs. Default CSP traffic per node per cycle: RPDO2 (controlword + target position, 6 B, ≤ 115 µs), TPDO2 (statusword + position actual, 6 B, ≤ 115 µs) and TPDO3 (statusword + velocity actual, 6 B, ≤ 115 µs). About 345 µs per node, plus a shared SYNC of 55 µs. SYNC rate Nodes Worst-case bus time / cycle Bus load @ 1 Mbit/s @ 500 kbit/s Verdict 1 kHz 1 400 µs 40 % 80 % OK at 1 M only 1 kHz 2 745 µs 75 % >100 % marginal (avoid) 500 Hz 2 745 µs 37 % 75 % OK 500 Hz 4 1435 µs 72 % >100 % marginal 250 Hz 4 1435 µs 36 % 72 % OK 250 Hz 8 2815 µs 70 % >100 % marginal Planning rule: keep the worst case at or below 60 % of the cycle, leaving room for SDO, EMCY and HB. CPU estimate per 1 kHz cycle on the C6: RX drain about 20 µs, SYNC/RPDO/TPDO processing about 40 µs, FSM and limits about 10 µs, six TMCL exchanges at 10 MHz SPI about 150 µs (to be measured, about 25 µs each in polling mode), AS5047U about 15 µs. That is roughly 235 µs, or 24 % CPU. The TMC9660 samples targets in a ~1 kHz internal loop that is not phase-locked to SYNC (Erratum 4 note, vortex_bench_safety.hpp:169 ), so expect up to 1 ms of extra transport delay. 1 kHz is the ceiling. 250–500 Hz is the recommended default for csp/csv/cst. 0x60C2 (interpolation time period) mirrors 0x1006, and drive_rt linearly interpolates targets when the SYNC period exceeds 1 ms.

docs.text: All PDOs are runtime-remappable in Pre-operational using the CiA 301 procedure: set COB-ID bit 31, set mapping sub0 = 0, write entries, set sub0 = n , clear bit 31. Mapping is limited to objects flagged mappable in the YAML, at most 8 entries, and the classic length limit of 8 bytes. The tool ships named profiles that apply a whole set in one command (§9.2). The suggested IDs are documented, and enabling them is an explicit configuration step (the imu-stream profile). RPDO2–4 have an RPDO timeout (event timer sub5) of 0 by default. The tool profiles set it to 3× the cycle.

docs.text: The drive refuses transition 4 (Switched On → Operation Enabled) with status bit 7 (warning) and EMCY 0x8100 unless at least one of these holds: 0x1016 consumes a heartbeat (≤ 500 ms), or the active mode's RPDO has an event timer (RPDO timeout), or the mode is cyclic and 0x1006 is non-zero (SYNC timeout monitored). This applies when 0x2701:03 "require master liveness" = 1 (the default). The deadman therefore always exists. Loss of any configured liveness source triggers the 0x6007 reaction: default 1 = Fault, which applies 0x605E. 0x1029:01 drives the NMT reaction. CANopenNode raises its own EMCYs (heartbeat consumer timeout, SYNC timeout, RPDO timeout) through CO_EM . The node translates them into FaultBook causes, so the 402 reaction and the journal entry come from the same table. Additionally, the TMC9660 SPI heartbeat monitor is enabled ( HEARTBEAT_MONITORING_CONFIG = SPI , timeout 20 ms; tmc9660_param_mode_tmcl.hpp:460 ). drive_rt exchanges with the chip at least every cycle, and at ≥ 100 Hz when idle. If the ESP32 hangs, crashes or is held in reset, the TMC9660 stops the bridge on its own ( HEARTBEAT_STOPPED flag) with the configured stop behaviour. That is the independent hardware path.
docs.title: 5.5 Liveness requirements for motion

docs.text: stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> NotReadyToSwitchOn NotReadyToSwitchOn --> SwitchOnDisabled: 1 (self-test ok) SwitchOnDisabled --> ReadyToSwitchOn: 2 shutdown ReadyToSwitchOn --> SwitchedOn: 3 switch on (config applied, limits valid) SwitchedOn --> OperationEnabled: 4 enable op (liveness gate, authority gate) OperationEnabled --> SwitchedOn: 5 disable op (0x605C) SwitchedOn --> ReadyToSwitchOn: 6 shutdown ReadyToSwitchOn --> SwitchOnDisabled: 7 quick stop / disable voltage OperationEnabled --> ReadyToSwitchOn: 8 shutdown (0x605B) OperationEnabled --> SwitchOnDisabled: 9 disable voltage SwitchedOn --> SwitchOnDisabled: 10 OperationEnabled --> QuickStopActive: 11 quick stop (0x605A) QuickStopActive --> SwitchOnDisabled: 12 stop done / disable voltage QuickStopActive --> OperationEnabled: 16 enable op (only option codes 5..8) OperationEnabled --> FaultReactionActive: 13 fault SwitchedOn --> FaultReactionActive: 13 ReadyToSwitchOn --> FaultReactionActive: 13 FaultReactionActive --> Fault: 14 reaction done (0x605E) Fault --> SwitchOnDisabled: 15 fault reset (cw bit7 rising, cause cleared) contracts/cia402_rules.hpp implements constexpr Decision Decide(State, ControlwordCmd, Inputs) . Inputs carries: fault active, authority ok, liveness ok, configuration valid, quick-stop done, velocity below threshold. It follows the pattern of pw_shared/system/clinical_lifecycle.hpp:166 : a single documented table, pure and host-tested. Controlword decode uses CiA 402 masks (shutdown xxxx x110 , switch on 0111 , enable 1111 , disable voltage xx0x , quick stop x01x , fault reset bit 7 edge). Statusword encode covers bits 0–6 per state, bit 7 warning, bit 9 remote (set when the controlword source holds authority), bit 10 target reached, bit 11 internal limit active and bits 12/13 per mode (pp: set-point ack / following error; hm: attained / error; csp/csv/cst: target ignored / following error). Transition 3 is where the OD application parameters are validated and pushed to the TMC9660, in the service slot. Transition 4 sets the commutation mode and asserts DRV_EN . Transitions out of Operation Enabled first set the TMC target to zero or ramp per the option code, and then switch commutation to SYSTEM_OFF or SYSTEM_OFF_LOW_SIDE_FETS_ON as the option code requires.
docs.title: 5.6 CiA 402 state machine as a rule table

docs.text: The approach follows pw-controller-sw/docs/software/bldc-motor-catalog.md : numbers live in one header of catalog rows. A SKU swap means picking a row id or uploading a custom row, never hunting through code. hal/.../config/VortexMotorCatalog.hpp holds constexpr rows: id, slug, tmcl::MotorType , pole pairs, rated/peak mA, Rs, Ls, Kt, max rpm, PWM Hz, default commutation, Hall/ABN data, safe tuning seeds. Row 0 is none . Row 1 is bench_24v_30w_bldc , seeded from vortex_bench_safety.hpp : 7 pole pairs, 390 µH, 25 kHz, 2.5 A max phase, I²t 2.5 A/2 s and 2.0 A/5 s. Further rows: generic_nema17_stepper , generic_brushed_dc , custom (all values from 0x3001–0x3008). 0x3000 selects a row. Selecting copies the row into 0x3001–0x3008 (application group), and the user may then edit. The OD stays the truth: the TMC9660's own NVM ( NvmStorage ) is not used. The chip is re-programmed from the OD at every transition 3. Feedback choices map to the TMC enums. Commutation: open-loop voltage/current, ABN, Hall, SPI encoder. Velocity and position sensors: same-as-commutation, Hall, ABN1, ABN2, SPI. The host AS5047U can serve as (a) an alignment and verification reference during commissioning, (b) an output-shaft absolute position in 0x60E4 (with 0x3009 gear ratio) for homing method 35/37 seeding, and © a plausibility monitor (commutation encoder vs. host encoder divergence → EMCY 0x7300-class). It cannot close the TMC loop unless the board routes it to the TMC SPI-encoder or ABI pins (Q5). The Hall/ABN bootloader mux ( BootloaderConfig ) depends on the board. It is a build-time board fact, held in the catalog's board section, not an OD object. Changing 0x3003 to a feedback whose pins are not muxed is rejected with SDO abort 0x06090030 (value range) and a hint code in 0x3021.
docs.title: 6.1 Motor and feedback catalog

docs.text: With factory defaults, row 0 ( none ) refuses transition 3 with EMCY 0x6320 ("parameter error") until a row is selected and stored. Limits clamp in three layers, and the effective value is the minimum: board limit (compile-time: shunt, MOSFET, connector rating) ≥ catalog row peak ≥ 0x6073/0x6072/0x60E0/0x60E1. Writes beyond the board limit abort with 0x06090031 (value too high). TMC protection (OV/UV, OT, OC, I²t) is always programmed from 0x3007 before DRV_EN . Torque mode (tq/cst) needs an explicit 0x6080 max motor speed. Exceeding it triggers quick stop with EMCY 0x8400-class ("velocity speed controller"), which prevents unloaded runaway (see the bench warning in BLDC_BRINGUP.md:71 ).

Coasting (code 0) is the only option when the bridge itself is faulted, and the arbiter downgrades the reaction automatically when the class is "Disable now".
docs.title: 6.4 Fault funnel and EMCY mapping

docs.text: LivenessMonitor (the same design as pw_shared/system/liveness_monitor.hpp ) has checkpoints for drive_rt (5 ms, critical), co_svc (50 ms, critical), i2c_io (100 ms, critical) and housekeep (1 s, non-critical). safety (every 5 ms) evaluates the verdict and raises RtStall / SvcStall causes. It feeds the ESP task watchdog only while the critical verdict is clean. Only safety subscribes to the TWDT, with the timeout reduced from 5 s to 500 ms. On a critical stall it commands, in order: TMC SYSTEM_OFF (if drive_rt is not the stalled thread), then DRV_EN low via i2c_io , then a journal entry, then it stops feeding the watchdog. Independent path: the TMC9660 SPI heartbeat (§5.5) and the hardware DRV_EN pull-down (verify on the schematic, Q6).
docs.title: 6.5 Safety arbiter and liveness-gated watchdog

docs.text: 0x4100 (raw TMCL bridge), the commissioning commands and 0x2601 secrets are gated twice. The writer must hold authority, and the node must be in Pre-operational or Switched On (never Operation Enabled).
docs.title: 6.6 Service-only objects

docs.text: Groups and keys: od_comm (0x1010:02), od_app (0x1010:03), od_cal (0x1010:04) in namespace vortex_cfg ; lss (node-ID, bit-rate index) in vortex_cfg ; secrets in vortex under a separate key; the fault journal ring in a new namespace vortex_log . The NVS partition should be encrypted ( nvs_flash_secure_init + flash encryption) if secrets are stored (Q8). Record format, versioned by OD address rather than memory layout. Header {magic VXOD , u16 format, u32 OD hash, u32 count, u32 crc32}, followed by TLV records {u16 index, u8 sub, u8 type, u8 len, value}. On restore, every record whose (index, sub, type) exists in the current OD with persist = its group is range-checked and applied. Unknown or invalid records are dropped and counted (0x2800). Missing ones keep defaults. Changing the OD therefore never bricks a stored configuration. A YAML migrations: list can map renamed addresses. CANopenNode integration: CO_storage_init with custom store / restore callbacks that serialise the TLV list for each entry group. This replaces CO_storageBlank.c . 0x1011 writes a "restore pending" flag, and defaults apply after the next reset (CiA 301 semantics). Store is refused in Operation Enabled (flash cache stall, §4.4) with abort 0x08000022 , and it runs in co_svc . LSS: CANopenNode's LSS slave store callback ( CO_LSSslave_initCfgStoreCallback ) writes lss . At boot the order is LSS-stored node-ID → Kconfig default → 0xFF (unconfigured, LSS only). The bit-rate index follows the CiA 305 table (0 = 1 M, 1 = 800 k, 2 = 500 k, 3 = 250 k, 4 = 125 k, 6 = 50 k, 7 = 20 k, 8 = 10 k). The CommChannelsManager hard-coded 500 kbit/s becomes the value read from lss , applied before EspCan init. "Activate bit timing" re-initialises the TWAI node after the switch delay.
docs.title: 6.7 Persistence

docs.text: Path Recommendation Why Wi-Fi STA + TLS tunnel (binary frame records) Primary wireless path (Phase 2) python-canopen works unchanged through a python-can bus plugin ( interface="vortex" , channel="tls://host:port" ), so the whole CLI and test suite runs over Wi-Fi. Throughput is high, and it is reachable from any PC on the LAN CiA 309-3 ASCII over TLS-TCP Optional (Phase 3) Human- and script-friendly (" [1] 5 r 0x6041 0 u16 "). CANopenNode ships CO_gateway_ascii.c and can address the whole CAN bus as a gateway. It is valuable for integrators and needs no special client ESP-NOW Secondary (Phase 3): a PC dongle (any ESP32-C6/S3 board running vortex-espnow-bridge firmware exposing slcan over USB-CDC), plus board-to-board links No AP is needed and latency is low. slcan is supported by python-can on all OSes, so the dongle looks like a USB-CAN adapter. The same frame-record codec is used BLE Commissioning only, if wanted (Q4): IDF network provisioning (security 2, SRP6a) to set Wi-Fi credentials Avoids typing secrets into SDO from a PC
docs.title: 7.1 Recommendation

docs.text: Datagram format: {u8 ver=1, u8 flags, u16 seq, u32 ack/epoch, then records: {u32 id|EXT|RTR, u8 flags FDF/BRS/ESI, u8 len, data[len]}...} . A record is the transport form of CanFrame , so FD lengths are already representable. Wi-Fi carries the stream over TLS 1.3 PSK (mbedTLS via esp-tls). ESP-NOW carries one datagram per action frame: ≤ 250 B for v1 compatibility, ≤ 1470 B with v2. That is up to 23 classic frames per v1 datagram. Records arrive at the router as from any other port (§4.3), with that port's policy.
docs.title: 7.2 Frame-record tunnel (shared by Wi-Fi and ESP-NOW)

docs.text: ESP-NOW: unicast only, CCMP-encrypted with a per-peer LMK under a device PMK. Broadcast or multicast cannot be encrypted, so the node ignores broadcast data except a signed pairing beacon. At most 17 encrypted peers; the IDF default is 7 ( CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_ESPNOW_MAX_ENCRYPT_NUM ). Keys are set over CAN or USB (0x2601, write-only) or by a pairing button sequence. An application sequence number with a replay window is added on top of CCMP. Wi-Fi: credentials are provisioned via 0x2601 or BLE provisioning. The TLS-PSK identity and key are per device. There is no plaintext listener. Auth failures are rate-limited and counted in 0x2602. mDNS advertises _vortex-co._tcp for discovery. NVS encryption is required whenever secrets are present (Q8).
docs.title: 7.3 Security

docs.text: By default 0x2701 allows enable (transition 4) from CAN only. A wireless writer of 0x6040 is accepted only for transitions towards safety (disable operation, disable voltage, quick stop). Shutdown/switch-on/enable (transitions ⅔/4) and fault reset are rejected with abort 0x08000022 . If a user sets 0x2701 to allow wireless enable, the wireless port must hold authority (0x2700 request/grant). It must send a deadman (tunnel keep-alive or HB mirror) at least every 0x2701:02 ms (default 200). On loss, the 0x6007 reaction applies. Authority changes only in Switched On or below. A request from another transport while one holds authority is refused. The CAN master can always revoke authority, because CAN wins. NMT from wireless is limited by default to Reset Node / Pre-operational (Stop and Start need policy). Wireless never writes 0x1010, 0x4100 or 0x2601 unless policy bit "wireless service" is set.
docs.title: 7.4 Safety rules (never bypass)

docs.text: What is abstracted now: CanFrame with len ≤ 64 plus FDF/BRS/ESI. PortCaps reports fd and max_len . The router enforces the per-port length. BaseCan v2 in hf-internal-interface-wrap gets an FD-sized message ( data[64] , byte length, flags). The FD flags stay on the current hf_can_message_t only after data is enlarged. Until then SetDLC > 8 must be rejected, which fixes the latent overrun (§3). CO_driver_target.h uses CO_CAN_MAX_LEN . Stack config CO_PDO_MAX_SIZE comes from one place. YAML mapping limits are per build ( fd_only objects are compiled out on classic). The PDO profile tables in contracts declare classic and FD variants. CiA 402-6 defines CANopen FD PDO mapping, and the FD variants follow it. On FD, one RPDO (controlword + target + offsets) and one TPDO (status + all actuals + error + temperatures, about 24 B) replace RPDO2–4 and TPDO2–4. At 1 / 5 Mbit/s this is about 70 µs per frame instead of 2–3 × 135 µs. What an STM32 FDCAN binding needs: StmFdcanPort : ICanPort with nominal and data bit timing, TDC ( SetTransmitterDelayCompensation , already in BaseCan ), RX FIFO interrupt → sink, TX FIFO non-blocking, bus-off auto-recovery policy, and hardware filter banks (FDCAN has many, so useCANrxFilters = true ). Stack: CANopenNode v4 has no CiA 1301. Its PDO path assumes ≤ 8 bytes in at least one place: bitwise-mapping copies CO_PDO_MAX_SIZE bytes into a uint64_t ( 301/CO_PDO.c:787-789 ). Mapping entries are limited to 8. Two options, decided when hardware exists (Q9): (a) Extend CANopenNode: 64-byte PDOs with bitwise mapping disabled, more mapping entries, an FD EMCY format and a new USDO server module. Upstream the work. (b) Replace the stack behind CoStack with a commercial CiA 1301 stack (for example emotas or MicroControl, which advertise CiA 1301). Either way the OD YAML, contracts, drive app, router and tools are unchanged. The generator gains an XDD (CiA 1311) emitter, and python tooling needs a USDO client. python-canopen has none today, so it would be a small added module. USDO uses the 0x600/0x580+id ranges with destination addressing in the payload, and it is not backward compatible with CiA 301 SDO. CiA 1301 is a separate network mode, not a per-frame option. A node runs either CANopen CC or CANopen FD on a given bus. The Kconfig/CMake option VORTEX_CANOPEN_FD selects the stack mode, and the YAML marks SDO vs USDO channel objects.
docs.title: 8. CAN FD readiness

docs.text: vortex_v1.eds is generated (§4.2) and checked in under od/ and inside the Python package. A firmware build embeds the OD hash (0x5FFE). vortex-canopen info warns if the device hash differs from the packaged EDS.

docs.text: Adapters: - Reference: PEAK PCAN-USB FD. It is isolated, has mature Windows/Linux drivers, is FD-ready for the STM32 future, and python-can pcan supports it. - Low-cost: candleLight-firmware adapters (CANable 2.x and similar) via gs_usb (Windows/macOS through libusb, Linux native SocketCAN). FD support depends on the adapter firmware. - Alternative: Kvaser Leaf v3. Wiring: twisted pair CAN_H/CAN_L plus signal ground. 120 Ω at each physical end, so the measured resistance between H and L with power off is 60 Ω. Stubs ≤ 0.3 m at 1 Mbit/s. Confirm whether Vortex has on-board termination or a jumper (Q7). Confirm the transceiver STB pin polarity and drive PCAL_CAN_HS_STB_OP to normal mode at boot (§3). # Test Pass criterion B1 Boot heartbeat at 125k/250k/500k/1M (set by LSS) HB every 100 ms ± 1 ms. No error frames over 10 min B2 scan , info , OD hash matches all objects readable B3 SDO block upload of 0x4001 (2 KB) and download of a DCF CRC ok, ≥ 20 kB/s at 1M B4 PDO remap to each profile mapping read-back equals profile B5 Bus-off: short H/L during traffic, release 0x8140 EMCY after recovery. Drive reacts per 0x6007 if it was in OE B6 Pull the adapter (heartbeat loss) in pv 0x8130, Fault within HB time + 1 cycle, shaft stops B7 demo pv / pp / tq (unloaded tq only with 0x6080 set) per catalog row profile tracks. Limits respected B8 demo csp at 250/500/1000 Hz with a Linux SocketCAN host RT step WCET ≤ 300 µs (0x4201). Following error within window B9 ESP32 hang (debug command to stop drive_rt ) TMC heartbeat stop within 20 ms (scope on phase current) B10 IMU stream TPDO5–7 at 100 Hz plus csp 500 Hz no TPDO late (0x8220/inhibit), bus load ≤ 60 % B11 Store/restore and power cycle parameters persist. 0x1011 restores defaults after reset

docs.text:
flowchart LR subgraph build["CMake host build (Linux)"] CORE["CANopenNode + OD.c (same files)"] APP["node app: CoNode, DriveAxis, Router, Safety"] SIM["HAL sims: SimAxisPort (motor model),
SimEncoder, SimImu, SimNvs, SimGpio"] PORT["LinuxSocketCanPort (vcan0)
or PipePort (fallback)"] end BIN["vortex_node_host --node-id 5 --port vcan0"] PY["pytest + python-canopen
(conformance-style suites)"] build --> BIN PY -->|"python-can socketcan / vortex pipe plugin"| BIN PY -->|"fault injection over a control socket"| SIM The host binary compiles the same CANopenNode sources, the generated OD.c , contracts and node application. Only the ICanPort binding, the HAL facade implementations and the RTOS shim differ (pthreads; BaseThread host stub as in pw-controller-sw/tests/host/SystemStateMachineThreadHostStub.cpp ). SimAxisPort models the TMC9660 behaviour the app relies on: an electrical/mechanical model (R, L, Kt, J, b, load torque), internal current/velocity/position PI with the TMC ramp, flags (OC, OV, UV, OT, I²t, Hall error, heartbeat stop), the ~1 kHz target sampling quirk and the SPI heartbeat. Faults are injected over a JSON control socket from pytest. Bus: GitHub-hosted runners do not reliably provide the vcan module. GitHub has said it has no plans to add kernel modules, and linux-modules-extra-$(uname -r) has been missing on some images ( community #26614 , #63910 ). The job tries modprobe vcan . If that fails, it uses PipePort : a UNIX-socket hub that carries the §7.2 frame records, with a matching python-can BusABC plugin. That plugin is the same one used for the Wi-Fi tunnel, so the codec is tested on every run. The suite is identical on both buses, and a self-hosted runner can force vcan . Suites (pytest, parametrised over bitrate-agnostic timing): Suite Checks test_nmt_hb.py boot-up message, NMT state transitions, HB period, 0x1F80 behaviour, reset comm/node test_sdo.py expedited (½/¾ B), segmented, block upload/download with CRC, abort codes (0x06020000 no object, 0x06010002 ro, 0x06070010 type length, 0x06090031 high, 0x08000022 state) test_pdo.py mapping procedure, invalid mapping aborts, sync/async/event timer/inhibit, RPDO timeout EMCY, length error EMCY test_sync_time_emcy.py SYNC consumer, window, SYNC timeout; TIME sets journal clock; EMCY inhibit; 0x1003 history and clear test_lss.py fastscan, set ID, set bit-rate, store, identity match test_storage.py 0x1010/0x1011 groups, refusal in OE, TLV migration fixtures (OD v n → v n +1) test_402_fsm.py every transition 0–16 from every state (table-driven from contracts), statusword bits, option codes 0x605A–0x605E, 0x6007 test_modes.py pp (set-point handshake bits ⅘/9, target reached), pv, tq (with speed limit), hm (methods 35/37, switch methods with sim REF), csp/csv/cst with host SYNC test_faults.py each policy-table row: inject → EMCY code/ER/402 reaction/journal entry/fault-reset rules/escalation test_authority.py wireless enable refused, policy grant, deadman loss, CAN revoke test_manufacturer_area.py IMU/encoder/temperature objects and packed PDO scaling test_cli.py vortex-canopen commands against the host node Contracts get C++ unit tests (GoogleTest, as in pw-controller-sw/tests/host ): the CiA 402 rule table, fault policy, TLV store codec, router policy and PDO profile tables.

docs.text: Vortex V1 Drive Observability: TMC9660 Telemetry, Diagnostics, Configuration and Visualisation ¶ Status Draft for owner review Date 2026-11-01 Companion canopen-node.md (the "CANopen design"). Section numbers prefixed "C§" refer to it Scope Everything the TMC9660 can report or be told, exposed through the Vortex CANopen object dictionary, the vortex-canopen CLI and a local web dashboard Code base read hf-tmc9660-driver@bc3cfcc , hf-hal-vortex-v1@28f1a63 ( ci/fix-workflows ), hf-core@54cbb5e , hardfoc-vortex-v1@0d98cde Paths are relative to the repository named in each section. Object indices are for axis 1. Axis n adds 0x400·( n −1) in the 0x3000–0x3FFF block, as C§5.3 says. 0. Summary ¶ The goal is a node that shows and controls every capability of the TMC9660 through one object dictionary (OD). The research produced five findings that shape the design: The chip surface is large, and it can now be enumerated mechanically. The driver's X-macro lists contain 288 axis parameters, 55 global parameters, 4 flag words (93 named bits) and 61 option enums: 865 rows in all. A small parser (Appendix B) reads them exhaustively and checks its own row count against the header. It also acts as a CI gate: every parameter must be bound to an OD object or explicitly excluded. Today 0 are unmapped and 42 are excluded (TMCL-script variables and UART addressing). SPI is the bottleneck. The CANopen design's budget of ~25 µs per TMCL access is not what the code does today. SpiCommInterface::transferTMCL ( inc/tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp ) puts a fixed kTmclPairGapUs = 1000 µs between the command frame and the reply-request frame. HalSpiTmc9660Comm::hostSpiTransferTMCLPair ( hf-hal-vortex-v1/lib/core/handlers/tmc9660/Tmc9660Handler.cpp:184-203 ) then adds DelayUs(200) . A parameter read therefore costs about 1.25 ms . On top of that, the NOT_READY retry budget allows up to 50 × 200 µs = 10 ms. Six accesses per SYNC would take about 7.5 ms, so 1 kHz CSP (C§4.5, R13) is impossible until this gap is characterised and reduced. Measuring and tuning it is the first implementation step (§7, PR 2b). Every budget below is given as a function of the per-access time, so the design holds whatever the measurement shows. PWM-rate signals can only come from the chip's own RAMDebug engine. Phase currents, FOC interim voltages, raw ADC values and the open-loop angle change at the PWM/FOC rate. No host polling can follow them. The TMC9660 has an on-chip capture engine (TMCL opcode 142, Table 16 transcribed in tmc9660_param_mode_tmcl.hpp:330-404 ) with parameter channels, a trigger with mask, shift and threshold, pre-trigger and a prescaler. The design therefore has two scope engines behind one OD interface : a host engine (cycle rate, any OD signal, free for signals already fetched) and a TMC engine (PWM-rate, chip parameters only). It also turns RAMDebug into a PWM-rate black box that is armed on gate-driver faults. The driver has defects that block the design. They are listed in §1.9. The RamDebug wrapper sends the wrong sub-commands and cannot configure channels. The Parameters enum aliases the global heartbeat parameters onto axis ids ¾, which are MOTOR_PWM_FREQUENCY / COMMUTATION_MODE . Heartbeat::configureAuto arms the UART watchdog on an SPI board. Firmware facts from the bench outweigh the datasheet. The FW051V100 parameter scans ( examples/esp32/docs/TMCL_PARAM_SCAN_*.md ) show which parameters answer before and after MOTOR_TYPE is set, which subsystems the bootloader gates, and which writes the ROM rejects (NR 245/246 gate currents, Y2 and VGS-short writes, I²t time constant < ~1 s). These become a firmware quirk profile that the configuration validator enforces (§4.3). The design adds 56 OD objects. Board-level objects are 0x2801 and 0x2900–0x2906. Axis objects are 0x3019, 0x3023–0x3024, 0x3030–0x3048 and 0x3100–0x3121. Service objects are 0x4300–0x4312. It adds eight new pytest suites in host CI. Its implementation PRs slot into C§10.2. 1. TMC9660 capability inventory ¶ 1.1 Method and sources ¶ Parameters: hf-tmc9660-driver/inc/parameter_mode/tmc9660_param_mode_tmcl.hpp . Each parameter group is an X-macro #define <GROUP>_LIST(X) with rows X(NAME, NR, /*!< doc */) . enum class Parameters (line 5227) includes 25 of these lists. Global banks 0/⅔ are separate lists (lines 457-596). Flag words use FLAG(bit) or literal masks (lines 4945-5215). Units: inc/tmc9660_units.hpp (k_RPM, acceleration factor, φe scale, MotorContext::cpr() ) and src/tmc9660.ipp (chip temperature T = raw·0.01615 − 268.15 , lines 4754-4756 and 5162-5164). Bench reality: hf-hal-vortex-v1/examples/esp32/docs/ ( TMCL_PARAM_SCAN_FAILURES.md , TMCL_PARAM_SCAN_POST_CONFIG.md , BLDC_BRINGUP.md , BLDC_UART_BRINGUP.md , TMC9660_DEEP_AUDIT_REPORT.md , TMC9660_FOC_ABN_DEEP_DIVE_REPORT.md ) and main/common/vortex_bench_safety.hpp , vortex_motor_bench_common.hpp . Vendor documents: TMC9660 datasheet https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/tmc9660.pdf , Parameter Mode Reference Manual https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/tmc9660-parameter-mode-reference-manual.pdf , AN-2601 Configuration and Bootstrapping https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/app-notes/an-2601.pdf , AN-2630 Addon Reference Guide https://www.analog.com/cn/resources/app-notes/an-2630.html , product page https://www.analog.com/en/products/tmc9660.html . During this research the analog.com fetches timed out. Vendor facts quoted here therefore come from the driver's transcriptions of the manual's tables (table numbers kept in the header comments) and from the audit reports that cite manual pages. Facts that need the PDF are marked (verify) . tools/tmcl_inventory.py (Appendix B) parses the header and asserts that the number of parsed rows equals the number of X( lines (865 = 865). It classifies every parameter and emits three outputs: the Appendix A tables, the YAML subs: for the TMC parameter image objects (§6), and a --check exit code for CI. 1.2 Inventory at a glance ¶ Class Count What it is OD home (a) live telemetry 54 read-only measurements, PI internals, encoder raw values, loop counters 0x3040–0x3045, CiA 402 actuals (b) status / diagnostic words 6 GENERAL_STATUS_FLAGS (289), GENERAL_ERROR_FLAGS (299), GDRV_ERROR_FLAGS (300), ADC_STATUS_FLAGS (301), ABN_1_INIT_STATE (93), VELOCITY_METER_MODE (139) 0x3030, 0x3043, health tree © configuration 264 (222 bound, 42 excluded) motor, gate driver, protection, ADC, feedback, loops, ramp, biquads, brake, stop events, homing, step/dir, globals 0x3100–0x3112 (TMC image) under engineering objects 0x3001–0x3009 (d) commands / targets 19 targets and offsets, commutation mode, brake release, I²t reset, ABN clear, SPI-encoder transfer/LUT, power-down CiA 402 objects, 0x3023, 0x3024 flag bits 93 31 status, 17 error, 31 gate-driver, 14 ADC clip per-bit counters 0x3034–0x3036 TMCL operations 48 Op enum: SAP/GAP/SGP/GGP/STAP/RFS/SIO/GIO/RamDebug/GetVersion/GetInfo/scripts/Boot §1.7 The full per-parameter tables with bank:id, access, CANopen type, SI scaling, rate tier and OD binding are in Appendix A, generated by the script. The curated tables below cover what the design depends on. Rate tiers used throughout: C = every drive_rt cycle (per SYNC); F = 50–100 Hz in rotating slots; S = 10 Hz; H = 1 Hz; X = scope/RAMDebug only (polling is meaningless at these rates); E = on demand (SDO snapshot); B = written at transition 3 and read back once. 1.3 Live telemetry (a): the signals that matter ¶ Signal TMCL (bank:id) Raw type SI Tier OD Position actual A:144 ACTUAL_POSITION I32 internal S (X while tuning) 0x3042 Electrical angles A:74 HALL_PHI_E , A:89 ABN_1_PHI_E , A:193 SPI angle, A:45 OPENLOOP_ANGLE I16 °e = v·360/65536 S / X 0x3043, 0x3044 Encoder raw A:100 ABN_1_VALUE , A:170 LAST_REFERENCE_POSITION I32 rev S / H 0x3043 Loop rates G0:12-14 MAIN/TORQUE/VELOCITY_LOOPS U32 /s loops/s H 0x3045 There is no PWM duty-cycle parameter. The duty cycle is derived from the FOC interim voltages (A:305-307) or from the d/q voltages (A:332), as the modulation index m = |U_dq| / U_full-scale (§1.4). It is published in 0x3046:03. 1.4 Units: what is solid and what still needs calibration ¶ Solid (driver math audited against the manual, TMC9660_DEEP_AUDIT_REPORT.md §2): currents in mA; supply in 0.1 V; chip temperature formula; k_RPM; acceleration register = (dv/dt)·2¹⁷/40 MHz (fixed in May 2026, docs/troubleshooting.md ); φe as 65536 per electrical revolution; break-before-make at 8.33 ns/LSB; drive time = (2v+3)/120 MHz; OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE 0..16383 = 0..100 % duty; I²t in A²·ms. One caveat: with a Hall sensor as the velocity source, the period meter reads 7/6 high ( tmc9660_units.hpp:178-181 ). Position stays exact. Internal units to calibrate (none of these is documented in the driver): Quantity Hypothesis Calibration step (bench, then frozen into 0x3048) 331/330 packed Iq/Id the same mA scale as ACTUAL_TORQUE without CURRENT_SCALING_FACTOR regress 331.hi against 105 over a torque sweep; store the A/LSB in 0x3048:05 332 packed Ud/Uq, A:305-307, A:314 full scale ±32767 corresponds to OUTPUT_VOLTAGE_LIMIT normalisation open-loop voltage mode at known OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE → compare; store V/LSB at 1 V bus in 0x3048:06 A:311-313, 315 FOC currents ADC-scaled current before mA conversion compare RAMDebug 311 against 105 at a steady state A:333/334 integration period summed per FOC or velocity loop read 333 twice with a known Δt at constant torque OUTPUT_VOLTAGE_LIMIT 32767 = 100 % circular limit sweep in open loop and observe U_dq saturation Until a calibration exists, the OD publishes these quantities as raw I16 with units: raw . The R32 SI versions in 0x3040 report NaN. 1.5 Status and diagnostic flags (b) ¶ All four words are read through GAP. The error and ADC words are write-1-to-clear ( Telemetry::clearGeneralErrorFlags , clearGateDriverErrorFlags , clearADCStatusFlags , inc/tmc9660.hpp Telemetry block). The status word mixes read-only state with read-write-clear latches (bits 4, 5, 11, 12, 14, 17). Word / bits Meaning Health node (§3) Use status b0–b3 regulation stopped / torque / velocity / position motor check that the commanded commutation mode is regulating. If b0 is set unexpectedly in Operation Enabled, the TMC fault handler has reverted to SYSTEM_OFF (the bench symptom in BLDC_BRINGUP.md ) status b4–b7 config stored/loaded, config/script memory read-only board expect 0 for stored and loaded (TMC NVM not used, §4.7). If loaded = 1 at boot → warning status b8, b21 brake chopper active, Y2 used for braking power duty statistics, regen energy status b9, b10, b15, b16 position/velocity reached, ramper velocity/position reached motor statusword bit 10 in pp/pv; ramp-done events status b11 ADC offset calibrated (clear to recalibrate) motor commissioning step 1; refuse transition 4 if 0 status b12, b13, b14, b17 ramper latched, switch stop, deviation stop, second move motor homing latches; deviation stop → 0x8611 status b18, b19 I²t ½ active motor statusword bit 11 (internal limit) status b20 reference search finished motor homing done status b23–b31 feature availability: StepDir, REF R/H/L, ABN2, Hall, ABN1, SPI flash, I²C EEPROM feedback / board validator input : the configured feedback must be available (§4.3) error b0, b1 config storage verify failed, TMCL script missing board journal only (both features unused) error b2 home switch not found motor homing error, statusword bit 13 in hm error b5 Hall invalid state feedback fault if Hall is the commutation or velocity source error b9 watchdog event board TMC reset detected → full re-apply (§4.5) error b13, b18 external temperature exceeded / warning power NTC on AIN3 error b14, b24 chip temperature exceeded / warning power error b16, b17 I²t limit ½ exceeded motor error b19, b20 supply OV / UV warning power error b21 ADC input over 2 V power warning, unused AINx (masked on the bench, kBenchOpenLoopIgnoredGeneralErrors ) error b22, b23 fault retry happened / all retries failed gate driver retry counter; retries failed → Fault error b26 heartbeat stopped comms the independent stop path (C§5.5) has acted gdrv b0–b3, b16–b19 low-/high-side overcurrent U/V/W/Y2 gate driver per-phase, per-side fault location gdrv b4–b11, b20–b27 discharge / charge (VGS) shorts per phase and side gate driver the spurious VGS trips on Vortex UVW ( BLDC_BRINGUP.md ) count here gdrv b12–b15 bootstrap undervoltage U/V/W/Y2 gate driver often caused by too-high duty with too-low PWM frequency gdrv b29–b31 gate-driver undervoltage, low voltage, supply undervoltage power VDRV rail ADC b0–b13 clipping on I0–I3, U0–U3, AIN0–3, VM, TEMP motor / power current-sense saturation (CSA gain too high) 1.6 Configuration ©: groups and their OD homes ¶ The CANopen design's engineering objects 0x3001–0x3009 stay (nameplate SI values from the catalog). Below them the design adds a TMC parameter image : one RECORD per driver group, with sub-indices in TMC units, generated from the header (§6.2). The image is normally derived from the engineering layer. Experts can pin individual sub-indices (0x3120), so the derivation does not overwrite them. Driver list (header) IDs Image object Derived from MOTOR_CONFIG_LIST (excl. 4) 0-3, 5, 8, 9 0x3100 0x3001 type, pole pairs, PWM Hz, scheme; 0x607E polarity GATE_DRIVER_LIST 233-249 0x3101 0x3002 ( PowerStageProfile math in the driver) UNDERVOLTAGE_/OVERCURRENT_/VGS_SHORT_PROTECTION_LIST 250-283 0x3102 0x3002 + quirk profile (VGS workaround) ADC_CONFIG_LIST (config part) 12, 17-37 0x3103 0x3002 shunt mΩ, peak A → CSA gain (highest with headroom), scaling factor TORQUE_FLUX_CONTROL_LIST (config part) 6, 7, 109-115, 308, 310 0x3104 0x3004, 0x6072/0x6073 clamps VELOCITY_CONTROL_LIST (loop part) 50, 51, 53, 67, 68, 123, 127-130, 133, 135, 137, 138 0x3105 0x3005, 0x3003 sensor POSITION_CONTROL_LIST (config part) 142, 145-149, 153, 155-157 0x3106 0x3006, 0x607D, 0x6067 VELOCITY_CONTROL_LIST (ramp part) 46, 47, 52, 54-66 0x3107 0x6081/0x6083/0x6084/0x6085 via k_rpm and the acceleration factor Hall (in FEEDBACK_SENSOR_CONFIG_LIST ) 75-85 0x3108 0x3003, commissioning 0x3022 ABN1 90-92, 94-98 0x3109 0x3003, 0x3022 ABN2 174-177 0x310A 0x3003, 0x3009 gear SPI encoder 181-184, 190, 191, 194-197, 201 0x310B 0x3003. G2:15 is reused as the configuration epoch token (§4.5). 1.7 Commands and procedures (d) ¶ TMCL op / parameter Use on Vortex OD / tool SAP 104/124/143 targets, 108/126 offsets cyclic set-points 0x6071, 0x60FF, 0x607A, 0x60B1/0x60B2 SAP 4 COMMUTATION_MODE owned by the CiA 402 FSM (transition 4 sets the mode; leaving Operation Enabled sets SYSTEM_OFF or SYSTEM_OFF_LOW_SIDE_FETS_ON ) read-back in 0x3030:07; service override 0x3023:06 (Switched On only) SAP 106/120 flux target/offset field-weakening experiments 0x3023:04/05 (service) SAP 216 RELEASE_BRAKE manual brake test 0x3023:01 SAP 230 RESET_IIT_SUMS after a cool-down or for tests 0x3023:02 SAP 99 ABN_1_CLEAR_ON_NEXT_NULL index-pulse homing (CiA methods 33/34) 0x3023:03 SAP 185-189, 198-199 SPI-encoder raw transfer, LUT upload 0x3024 DOMAIN procedure RFS (13) start/stop/status TMC reference search for homing methods 17-30 driven by hm mode, status in 0x3043:11 SGP/GGP bank 0 heartbeat, IO, wake 0x3112 SGP G0:11 power-down refused (wakes need board support) 0x3023:07 returns abort 0x06090030 SIO/GIO TMC GPIO17/18, AIN reads (NTC) 0x2400 (C§5.3), TemperatureManager RamDebug (142) types 0-14 TMC scope engine and PWM-rate fault capture 0x4300-0x4312 GetVersion (136) / GetInfo (157) identity 0x2002 STAP / FactoryDefault / script ops / Boot not used at runtime (§4.7). Raw access only through the 0x4100 bridge in service state — 1.8 Read cost model and measurement plan ¶ The cost of one TMCL access on SPI is T_op = 2·T_frame + T_gap + T_post , where T_frame ≈ CS setup + 64 bits at 10 MHz (6.4 µs) + IDF transaction overhead (about 10–15 µs). Measure it; do not assume it. Pipelining: transferTMCL(..., second_command) already lets the second frame of access k carry the command of access k +1, so a batch of N accesses costs about N·(T_gap + T_frame) + T_frame + T_post . Scenario T_gap T_post One access Batch of 6 (pipelined) Batch of 8 A: today ( kTmclPairGapUs , HAL DelayUs(200) ) 1000 µs 200 µs ≈ 1.24 ms ≈ 6.3 ms ≈ 8.4 ms B: conservative 250 µs 0 ≈ 290 µs ≈ 1.6 ms ≈ 2.2 ms C: target 50 µs 0 ≈ 90 µs ≈ 440 µs ≈ 580 µs D: best case (parser keeps up) 10 µs 0 ≈ 50 µs ≈ 200 µs ≈ 260 µs Measurement plan (bench app vortex_tmcl_timing , PR 2b): Instrument HalSpiTmc9660Comm::hostSpiTransferTMCLPair with esp_timer_get_time() around each frame and the gap. Count NOT_READY (0xF0) and 0x00 retries per access. Sweep T_gap ∈ {1000, 500, 250, 100, 50, 25, 10} µs and T_post ∈ {200, 50, 0} µs, in three chip states: SYSTEM_OFF , open-loop current mode at 25 kHz PWM, and FOC (Hall or ABN) under load. Run 10⁵ GAP reads of 125/105/289 at each point. Record the latency histogram (p50/p99/max), the retry count and any value mismatch against a slow reference read. Repeat the chosen point with pipelined batches of 6 and 8. Read G0:12 MAIN_LOOPS in each state. If the TMCL parser is serviced in the chip's main loop, the minimum safe gap tracks 1/ MAIN_LOOPS , so this is the number to report upstream. Pass criterion for a default: 10⁶ accesses with zero corrupt values and p99 retries ≤ 1. Publish the result as the new T_op and update C§4.5. Rules that hold whatever the outcome: Inside drive_rt , a gap longer than about 30 µs must not busy-wait at priority 24. Use a gptimer one-shot plus a task notification, or split the batch across the cycle. The NOT_READY budget inside drive_rt is at most 2 retries. After that the sample is marked stale (0x3041:14 sample age). A stale streak longer than 0x3047:06 cycles raises the "TMC link degraded" cause (§3.3), not a hang. Every TMC access in drive_rt records its latency into 0x3037. 1.9 Driver defects and gaps found (must fix before relying on them) ¶ # Finding Evidence Fix (PR 2a) D1 RamDebug::startCapture sends type 6 ( SET_TRIGGER_MASK_SHIFT ) instead of 7 ( ENABLE_TRIGGER ). readData uses opcode ReadMem instead of RamDebug type 9 READ_SAMPLE . getStatus treats any non-zero state as running, but COMPLETE = 3. There is no API for channels, trigger, prescaler or pre-trigger src/tmc9660.ipp:5365-5395 against Table 16/17 in tmc9660_param_mode_tmcl.hpp:330-420 full RAMDebug API ( configure(Channels, Trigger, prescaler, samples, pre) , state() , info(kind) , readSamples(span) ) D2 enum class Parameters includes HEARTBEAT_MONITORING_LIST (ids 3, 4) and HIBERNATION_WAKEUP_LIST (10, 11). These are global bank-0 parameters, and ¾ collide with MOTOR_PWM_FREQUENCY / COMMUTATION_MODE . writeParameter(Parameters::HEARTBEAT_MONITORING_TIMEOUT, 20) would SAP the commutation mode tmc9660_param_mode_tmcl.hpp:5227-5300 ; duplicate-id check in the script remove them from Parameters , keep only GlobalParamBank0 . Add a static_assert for unique axis ids D3 Heartbeat::configureAuto selects TMCL_UART_INTERFACE when enabled. On the SPI-connected Vortex the watchdog would then never see traffic, or would never trip src/tmc9660.ipp:5447-5461 take the interface explicitly. Vortex uses configure(SPI_INTERFACE, 20) D4 Fixed 1000 µs pair gap and 200 µs post-delay. The 10 ms NOT_READY budget suits only thread context tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp transferTMCL ; Tmc9660Handler.cpp:180,201 make gap, post-delay and retry budget per-call parameters. Add readParameters(span<ids>, span<out>) that pipelines D5 Doc comments disagree with the enums ( getMotorContext says NR 8/9/132 for ids 0/1/123). The FOC_ABN report uses other numbers src/tmc9660.ipp:4832-4852 ; TMC9660_FOC_ABN_DEEP_DIVE_REPORT.md §1 the header enums are canonical (they match the 263 OK reads in the post-config scan). Fix the comments D6 134 of 288 axis rows carry no access tag in the driver doc string, and the ADC clip flags have no description Appendix A "RW*" add a 4 th X-macro column ACCESS and a units string. The script then needs no heuristics D7 No wrapper for IPD/HFI sensorless start, index latching or I²t remaining time TMC9660_DEEP_AUDIT_REPORT.md §5 items 8, 9, 11 out of scope here; noted for the roadmap 1.10 Firmware facts that become rules (FW051V100, silicon rev 1 var 2) ¶ Before MOTOR_TYPE is set, 259 GAPs return REPLY_WRONG_TYPE . After MOTOR_TYPE = BLDC , 263 axis parameters read OK ( TMCL_PARAM_SCAN_POST_CONFIG.md ). The apply order must therefore set the motor type first. That is 5 TMCL accesses. Rotating slots (default R = 2 per cycle): a static, precomputed table serves the F/S/H tiers. At 500 Hz, R = 2 gives 1000 accesses/s: for example 10 F signals × 50 Hz = 500, 21 S signals × 10 Hz = 210, 10 H signals × 1 Hz = 10, with 280 to spare. The table is generated at transition 3 from 0x3047 and the selected feedback (no Hall reads when Hall is unused). A FAULTN edge (PCAL95555 GPIO_PCAL_TMC_FAULT_STATUS → INT → i2c_io ) preempts the rotation: on the next cycle the rotating slots read 299, 300 and 301. Service slot (S = 2 per cycle in Operation Enabled, up to 16 otherwise): configuration apply and verify, RAMDebug arm/poll/readout, on-demand SDO GAPs (an SDO read of 0x3044:xx outside the scope), and the 0x4100 bridge. Required SPI time per cycle = (5 + R + S)·(T_gap + T_frame) + T_frame + AS5047U ≈ 9·(T_gap + 20) + 35 µs. Scenario SPI time / cycle Max SYNC rate with SPI ≤ 50 % of cycle Recommended A (today) ≈ 9.2 ms ≈ 55 Hz not usable for cyclic modes. Profile modes at 10 ms with R = 0, S = 1 B ≈ 2.5 ms ≈ 200 Hz 100–200 Hz C ≈ 665 µs ≈ 750 Hz 500 Hz (C§4.5 default) D ≈ 305 µs ≈ 1.6 kHz (capped at 1 kHz by Erratum 4) 1 kHz When the cycle cannot fit R + S, drive_rt drops service work first, then rotating slots. It never drops fixed slots. It counts each drop in 0x3037:09/10. The scheduler is a pure function in contracts ( TelemetrySchedule Build(Rates, Feedback, Mode, BudgetUs) ), which host tests cover. 2.3 Telemetry snapshot and freshness ¶ drive_rt publishes a TelemetryFrame (about 160 B) through a seqlock, one per cycle. Every value carries the cycle number of its last successful read, so consumers know its age. 0x3041:14 is the age in cycles of the oldest fixed-slot value. TPDOs read the frame from the previous cycle, as C§4.4 specifies. At 500 Hz that is 2.05 s. drive_rt writes it every cycle in about 1 µs. Freeze: when FaultBook activates a cause of class Fault or Disable-now, the ring records 0x4310:02 post-trigger milliseconds (default 200), then freezes into slot 0 (latest) and, the first time after boot, also into slot 1. A frozen snapshot cannot be overwritten until it is read or cleared (0x4310:01 = 3). The journal entry (C§6.4) gets the snapshot sequence number. PWM-rate black box: while the user scope is idle, the TMC engine stays armed in fault-capture mode. Channels are 311/312/313 (FOC currents), 305 (U voltage) and 300 (GDRV flags). The trigger channel is 300, rising unsigned with threshold 0 and mask 0xFFFFFFFF. Pre-trigger is 75 %. On a gate-driver fault the chip itself holds the waveforms around the event. After the drive has stopped, drive_rt reads them out in the service slot into slot 2 of 0x4311. (Verify on the bench that a channel can trigger on parameter 300 and that RAMDebug keeps running after the fault handler has stopped the bridge.) Policy 0x4310:04 decides whether a user capture may pre-empt the black box (default yes, and the dashboard shows that the black box is off). Persistence: a snapshot is written to NVS vortex_log only outside Operation Enabled, which is the journal rule (C§4.4). Each record is ≤ 8 KiB, and one is kept. The readout is 0x4311 DOMAIN in the §2.5 format with engine = 2 (cycle snapshot) or 3 (black box). 0x4312 lists the slots (sequence number, time, cause, size). 3. Diagnostics model ¶ 3.1 Health tree ¶ flowchart TB B["board 0x2901\nESP32 die temp, heap, reset reason,\nthread liveness, NVS, TMC identity"] --> P["power 0x2902\nVbus, OV/UV warn, PCAL power-good,\nVDRV/gdrv supply UV, brake chopper, NTC"] P --> G["gate driver 0x2903 (rollup) / 0x3031\nOC per phase+side, VGS shorts,\nbootstrap UV, retries"] G --> M["motor 0x2904 / 0x3032\nI2t, chip temp, current clipping,\nregulation state, following error"] M --> F["feedback 0x2905 / 0x3033\nHall, ABN init, SPI enc, AS5047U,\nangle plausibility, IMU"] B --> C["comms 0x2906\nCAN TEC/REC, bus-off, HB consumer, SYNC,\nRPDO timeout, TMC SPI link, wireless"] The ordering expresses causality for the "root-cause" view. A child's fault is shown as caused by the parent when the parent faulted in the same or the previous cycle. For example, bootstrap undervoltage during a Vbus sag is attributed to power, not the gate driver. Each node is a RECORD with the same layout: Sub Name Type Meaning 1 status U8 0 unknown, 1 ok, 2 warning, 3 fault, 4 not fitted / disabled 2 active causes U32 bitmask of this node's cause ids (node-local numbering, decoded by the tool) 3 latched causes U32 OR since the last clear (write 0 to clear) 4 fault count U32 number of Fault-class activations since boot 5 warning count U32 6 last EMCY code U16 7 last event uptime U32 ms 8 worst value I32 node-specific (max temperature 0.1 °C, min Vbus 0.1 V, max I²t %, max following error, max TEC) 9 worst value uptime U32 ms 0x2900 is the summary: sub1–6 hold the node statuses, sub7 is a U32 packed rollup (4 bits per node, PDO-mappable, sent on change) and sub8 clears all latches (write 0x726C6300 ). Gate driver, motor and feedback are per axis (0x3031–0x3033). 0x2903–0x2905 are the worst-of over all axes. Configuration model ¶ 4.1 Two layers, one truth ¶ flowchart LR CAT["catalog row 0x3000"] --> ENG["engineering layer 0x3001-0x3009\n(SI: A, Ohm, H, Hz, V, degC)"] COM["commissioning results 0x3022\n(accept)"] --> ENG ENG -->|"derive (pure, contracts)"| IMG["TMC image 0x3100-0x3112\n(TMC units)"] PIN["pin mask 0x3120\n(expert overrides)"] --> IMG IMG -->|"apply at transition 3"| CHIP["TMC9660 RAM"] CHIP -->|"read-back"| VER["verify 0x3019"] The engineering layer is the user's view. It keeps the CANopen design's 0x3001–0x3009 objects, refined to carry the extra nameplate data the derivation needs: Rs, Ls, Kt, J (optional), peak and continuous current, shunt, FET Qg/Rds(on), target current-loop bandwidth. The TMC image is the chip's view. It is generated from the header (one sub-index per TMC parameter, §6.2). derive(Eng, BoardFacts, QuirkProfile) → Image is a pure function in contracts/tmc_image.hpp . It contains the driver's auto-config math ( CurrentSensing::configureAuto gain choice, GateDriver power-stage profile, Protection::configureAuto I²t and threshold encoding, Ramp k_rpm/acceleration conversion). The firmware therefore no longer calls the driver's configureAuto helpers at runtime. It applies a precomputed image. Host tests cover the math. Pinning: 0x3120 is an ARRAY U32[19], one bitmask per image object. A set bit means "keep the user's value and do not re-derive it". Any SDO write to an image sub-index sets its pin bit automatically. params unpin <obj> clears it. The parameter editor (§5.3) shows pinned values with a marker. Persistence: both layers persist in group A ( od_app ). Calibration-type results (Hall offsets, ABN N-offset, ADC offsets once accepted) persist in group K. The image is saved too, so a DCF reproduces a drive exactly even if a later firmware changes the derivation. On restore with a newer firmware, un-pinned sub-indices are re-derived and pinned ones are kept. 4.2 Validation rules ¶ Writes are validated in two passes: On SDO write (od_extension): data type, the YAML low / high range and access. Violations abort 0x06090031/0x06090032/0x06090030, as C§6.2 specifies. At transition 3 , over the whole image. The failure code goes to 0x3019:03 and the first offending object/sub-index to 0x3019:04. The transition is refused with EMCY 0x6320. Code Rule 0x01 range: every image value inside the inventory range (Appendix A) 0x02 MAX_TORQUE (6) ≤ min(board limit, catalog peak, 0x6073 · rated). MAX_FLUX (7) ≥ OPENLOOP_CURRENT (46) whenever an open-loop or forced-φe ABN init is configured ( vortex_bench_safety.hpp kMaxFluxCurrentMa note) 0x03 supply: UV warn (292) < nominal < OV warn (291) < brake-chopper limit (213) + hysteresis (214) < board absolute maximum 0x04 temperature: warning < shutdown for chip (298/297) and external (295/294); external thresholds converted from °C with the NTC curve 0x05 I²t: time constants ≥ 1000 ms (ROM floor); limit 1 ≥ limit 2 scaled by time (window 1 is the shorter one) 0x06 PWM 10–100 kHz; OUTPUT_VOLTAGE_LIMIT ≤ 32767; dead time (235/236) ≥ the FET requirement from 0x3002 0x07 feedback: the commutation mode, velocity sensor (123) and position sensor (142) must each be fitted (status b27–b29 availability) and muxed by the bootloader ( DeviceCapabilities , the BootloaderConfig board fact). ABN STEPS > 0 when ABN is selected. SPI-encoder sub-indices only if spiEncoder 0x08 Y2: no Y2 sub-index differs from the default when y2Phase = false (Vortex) 0x09 quirk profile (keyed by TMC FW id in 0x2002): skip NR 245/246 on FW051V100 unless the user pinned them and set 0x3121:03 "allow"; VGS-short UVW policy (disable or max deglitch) applied 0x0A position: limit low < limit high; POSITION_REACHED_THRESHOLD consistent with 0x6067 0x0B ramp: RAMP_VMAX ≥ the motor-side speed implied by 0x607F and the gear ratio; RAMP_VSTOP ≥ 1 0x0C heartbeat: config = SPI; timeout ≥ 3 × the idle drive_rt period and ≤ 50 ms 0x0D globals: AUTO_START_ENABLE = 0, CLEAR_USER_VARIABLES = 1 0x0E verify mismatch (§4.4) 0x0F TMCL error during apply (the reply code goes to 0x3019:05) 4.3 Apply order at transition 3 ¶ The order follows the proven bench sequence ( BENCH_MATRIX.md "TMC9660 BLDC bring-up shape", configure_complete_bldc ) and the firmware facts in §1.10. It runs in the drive_rt service slot with S raised to 16 accesses per cycle, because the bridge is off. The statusword stays in Ready to Switch On until the apply finishes. 0x3019:01 shows progress. Step Writes Notes 0 read G2:15 epoch, error b9, FW id decides between full and differential apply (§4.5) 1 A:4 = SYSTEM_OFF 2 0x3100 motor (type first , then pole pairs, direction, PWM, scheme, idle behaviour, voltage limit) before the motor type is set, most other parameters answer WRONG_TYPE 3 0x3101 gate driver (UVW only, quirk skips) 4 0x3102 protection (UVLO, OC, VGS) Vortex VGS policy 5 0x3103 current sensing 6 0x3108–0x310B the selected feedback only 7 0x3104 current loop, 0x3105 velocity loop, 0x3106 position loop, 0x310C biquads 8 0x3107 ramp and open-loop 9 0x310D protection (supply warnings, temperatures, I²t, fault handling) 10 0x310E brake, 0x310F stop events/switches, 0x3110 reference search, 0x3111 step/dir 11 0x3112 globals (SGP): heartbeat SPI + timeout last among the globals, so that a slow apply does not trip it 12 clear error/gdrv/ADC flags (write-1-clear all) 13 ADC offset calibration if status b11 = 0 (motor stationary) 14 read-back verify (§4.4) 15 write G2:15 = CRC32(image) epoch token Transition 4 then writes the target to zero, sets DRV_EN (PCAL), sets the commutation mode and reads back A:4 and status b0–b3 within 20 ms, else Fault 0xFF50. That is the C§5.6 behaviour plus the revert check. Time estimate: about 230 writes + 230 reads + flag clears ≈ 470 accesses. Scenario A: ≈ 0.6 s. Scenario C with S = 16 at 500 Hz: ≈ 60 ms. 4.4 Read-back verification ¶ Every RW/RWE sub-index that was written is read back with GAP/GGP. Write-only parameters (230) and RWC latches are skipped. A tolerance table covers parameters that the chip rounds or normalises. For example, MOTOR_PWM_FREQUENCY is accepted within ±1 % (verify which parameters are rounded by observing them on the bench, and record them in the quirk profile). The result is in 0x3019: verified count, mismatch count, first mismatch (index, sub, wanted, got) and the TMCL reply code. A mismatch refuses transition 3 (code 0x0E). diag config and the parameter editor show the full mismatch list, which the tool fetches by re-reading 0x3100–0x3112 against the stored image. 4.5 Differential apply and TMC reset detection ¶ G2:15 (a TMCL-script user variable that Vortex does not need for scripts) holds the CRC32 of the last applied image. CLEAR_USER_VARIABLES = 1 makes the chip clear it on reset. At the next transition 3: If G2:15 = CRC(last applied), WATCHDOG_EVENT = 0 and the chip has not been reset (no bootloader re-entry since the last apply), then only the sub-indices that changed since the last apply are written and verified. This is typically a few gains during tuning, which keeps tuning iterations under 50 ms. Otherwise the full apply runs. A mismatch that appears while the drive is enabled means the TMC reset under us: Fault 0x6010 (§3.3). 4.6 DCF export and import, diff against stored and defaults ¶ Export ( params export dcf FILE ): python-canopen uploads every object whose YAML persist is app , cal or comm . That includes the image and the pin masks. It writes a CiA 306 DCF with [DeviceComissioning] (node-ID, bit-rate, node name). Comments record the OD hash (0x5FFE), the firmware build (0x2000) and the TMC FW id (0x2002). The library function is canopen.objectdictionary.export_od(od, f, doc_type="dcf") . Import ( params import dcf FILE [--store] ): this refuses unless the drive is in Pre-operational or Switched On and holds authority (C§6.6). It checks the OD hash. If the hash differs, it maps by (index, sub, name) and reports dropped entries, which is the same rule as the TLV restore (C§6.7). It writes the engineering layer, then the pin masks, then the pinned image sub-indices. It optionally calls 0x1010:03/:04. Diff: the device exposes the stored TLV blobs read-only as 0x2801:01–03 DOMAIN (comm/app/cal). The tool decodes them with the same codec as the firmware (the Python port is shared in the package and tested against C++ fixtures). It then shows three columns: live / stored / default (from the EDS). The dashboard parameter editor uses the same data. 4.7 TMC9660 non-volatile memory is not used ¶ The OD is the single truth. The chip is reprogrammed at every transition 3 (C§6.1). Storing on the chip would create a second truth that could diverge silently. NvmStorage::storeToFlash (STAP 0xFFF) needs external SPI flash or I²C EEPROM configured through the bootloader ( inc/tmc9660.hpp NvmStorage warning). The Vortex SPI boot configuration has enable_flash = false , so the SPI port stays free for TMCL ( TMCL_PARAM_SCAN_POST_CONFIG.md table). Enforcement: STAP, FactoryDefault and the script opcodes are refused by the 0x4100 bridge unless a build flag VORTEX_TMC_EXPERT is set. At boot, status b5 CONFIG_LOADED = 1 raises the "unexpected TMC NVM config" warning, because someone used the vendor tool on this board. AUTO_START_ENABLE = 0 guarantees that no stored script runs. 5. Visualisation ¶ 5.1 CLI additions ( vortex-canopen , C§9.2) ¶ Command Function Data path plot SIG... A random session token is printed in the URL and checked on REST and WebSocket. There is one NodeSession per bus, and it uses the same transport options as the CLI ( --interface/--channel or --url ). SignalHub subscribes to TPDO callbacks and to EMCY/heartbeat. It decodes values with the catalog and pushes them to subscribed clients in 33 ms batches (msgpack: {sig_id: [t0, dt, values...]} ). SdoJobQueue serialises SDO jobs (snapshot polls, scope fetches, parameter reads/writes) with priorities, so a 32 KiB block upload cannot starve the 2 Hz health poll. Frontend: a static single-page app built at release time and shipped inside the wheel (no Node.js at install). It uses Svelte for the UI, uPlot ( https://github.com/leeoniya/uPlot ) for all time-series and FFT plots (it renders tens of thousands of points per frame), and three.js for the IMU attitude. Library versions are pinned in package-lock.json . The bundle must work offline. Safety: without --allow-control the dashboard is read-only. Commands that can move the motor (wizard steps, enable, tune steps) are hidden. The server refuses any write to 0x6040, 0x3020, 0x3023 or 0x3100–0x3112. With --allow-control , motion buttons need a confirmation and use the same authority rules as the CLI (C§7.4). The page shows a persistent "control enabled" banner and a large quick-stop button that writes 0x6040 = quick stop. Recording: any panel can record to Parquet (signals plus EMCY/state events) via a toolbar button. The recordings replay in the same UI ( dash --replay FILE ). 5.3 Panels (wireframes, data sources, rates) ¶ P1 Drive state machine +-- Drive ------------------------------------------------------------+ | [NotReady]->[SwOnDisabled]->[Ready]->[SwitchedOn]->[(OpEnabled)] | | ^ fault reset [QuickStop] [FaultReact]->[Fault] | mode: csv (0x6061) cw 0x000F sw 0x0637 authority: CAN liveness: HB ok | warn: I2t1 active | target reached | internal limit | | [Shutdown] [Switch on] [Enable] [Quick stop] [Fault reset] (control) | +---------------------------------------------------------------------+ Sources: TPDO1 (0x6041/0x6061, event, ≤ 100 Hz), 0x2700, 0x603F, 0x4003. OD additions (YAML fragment for od/vortex_od.yaml ) ¶ 6.1 Conventions ¶ The keys are the C§4.2 attributes: name (ParameterName), object_type (VAR/ARRAY/RECORD/DOMAIN), data_type , access , pdo_mapping , default , low / high , units , persist ( comm|app|cal|none ), od_extension , fd_only and docs . The fragment adds two keys, which odgen must learn: tmc: {bank: axis|0|2, id: N} binds a sub-index to a TMC parameter. The TmcParamGroup / TmcTelemetry extensions use it to find the parameter. tmcl_inventory.py --check uses it to prove coverage. source: snapshot|service|ram says where an od_extension serves the value from. snapshot means the drive_rt seqlock frame, with no SPI on read. service means a GAP in the service slot, so the SDO response is deferred. ram means node RAM. Sub-index 0 of RECORD and ARRAY objects is implicit (highest sub-index), as in CANopenNode v4. Names are snake_case. odgen derives the ParameterName from them. pdo_mapping: true is only set where the classic 8-byte limit allows a useful mapping. The indices are for axis 1. docs.text: The goal is a node that shows and controls every capability of the TMC9660 through one object dictionary (OD). The research produced five findings that shape the design: The chip surface is large, and it can now be enumerated mechanically. The driver's X-macro lists contain 288 axis parameters, 55 global parameters, 4 flag words (93 named bits) and 61 option enums: 865 rows in all. A small parser (Appendix B) reads them exhaustively and checks its own row count against the header. It also acts as a CI gate: every parameter must be bound to an OD object or explicitly excluded. Today 0 are unmapped and 42 are excluded (TMCL-script variables and UART addressing). SPI is the bottleneck. The CANopen design's budget of ~25 µs per TMCL access is not what the code does today. SpiCommInterface::transferTMCL ( inc/tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp ) puts a fixed kTmclPairGapUs = 1000 µs between the command frame and the reply-request frame. HalSpiTmc9660Comm::hostSpiTransferTMCLPair ( hf-hal-vortex-v1/lib/core/handlers/tmc9660/Tmc9660Handler.cpp:184-203 ) then adds DelayUs(200) . A parameter read therefore costs about 1.25 ms . On top of that, the NOT_READY retry budget allows up to 50 × 200 µs = 10 ms. Six accesses per SYNC would take about 7.5 ms, so 1 kHz CSP (C§4.5, R13) is impossible until this gap is characterised and reduced. Measuring and tuning it is the first implementation step (§7, PR 2b). Every budget below is given as a function of the per-access time, so the design holds whatever the measurement shows. PWM-rate signals can only come from the chip's own RAMDebug engine. Phase currents, FOC interim voltages, raw ADC values and the open-loop angle change at the PWM/FOC rate. No host polling can follow them. The TMC9660 has an on-chip capture engine (TMCL opcode 142, Table 16 transcribed in tmc9660_param_mode_tmcl.hpp:330-404 ) with parameter channels, a trigger with mask, shift and threshold, pre-trigger and a prescaler. The design therefore has two scope engines behind one OD interface : a host engine (cycle rate, any OD signal, free for signals already fetched) and a TMC engine (PWM-rate, chip parameters only). It also turns RAMDebug into a PWM-rate black box that is armed on gate-driver faults. The driver has defects that block the design. They are listed in §1.9. The RamDebug wrapper sends the wrong sub-commands and cannot configure channels. The Parameters enum aliases the global heartbeat parameters onto axis ids ¾, which are MOTOR_PWM_FREQUENCY / COMMUTATION_MODE . Heartbeat::configureAuto arms the UART watchdog on an SPI board. Firmware facts from the bench outweigh the datasheet. The FW051V100 parameter scans ( examples/esp32/docs/TMCL_PARAM_SCAN_*.md ) show which parameters answer before and after MOTOR_TYPE is set, which subsystems the bootloader gates, and which writes the ROM rejects (NR 245/246 gate currents, Y2 and VGS-short writes, I²t time constant < ~1 s). These become a firmware quirk profile that the configuration validator enforces (§4.3). The design adds 56 OD objects. Board-level objects are 0x2801 and 0x2900–0x2906. Axis objects are 0x3019, 0x3023–0x3024, 0x3030–0x3048 and 0x3100–0x3121. Service objects are 0x4300–0x4312. It adds eight new pytest suites in host CI. Its implementation PRs slot into C§10.2.

Each parameter group is an X-macro #define <GROUP>_LIST(X) with rows X(NAME, NR, /*!< doc */) . enum class Parameters (line 5227) includes 25 of these lists. Global banks 0/⅔ are separate lists (lines 457-596). Flag words use FLAG(bit) or literal masks (lines 4945-5215). Units: inc/tmc9660_units.hpp (k_RPM, acceleration factor, φe scale, MotorContext::cpr() ) and src/tmc9660.ipp (chip temperature T = raw·0.01615 − 268.15 , lines 4754-4756 and 5162-5164). During this research the analog.com fetches timed out. Vendor facts quoted here therefore come from the driver's transcriptions of the manual's tables (table numbers kept in the header comments) and from the audit reports that cite manual pages. Facts that need the PDF are marked (verify) . tools/tmcl_inventory.py (Appendix B) parses the header and asserts that the number of parsed rows equals the number of X( lines (865 = 865). It classifies every parameter and emits three outputs: the Appendix A tables, the YAML subs: for the TMC parameter image objects (§6), and a --check exit code for CI.

docs.text: Solid (driver math audited against the manual, TMC9660_DEEP_AUDIT_REPORT.md §2): currents in mA; supply in 0.1 V; chip temperature formula; k_RPM; acceleration register = (dv/dt)·2¹⁷/40 MHz (fixed in May 2026, docs/troubleshooting.md ); φe as 65536 per electrical revolution; break-before-make at 8.33 ns/LSB; drive time = (2v+3)/120 MHz; OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE 0..16383 = 0..100 % duty; I²t in A²·ms. One caveat: with a Hall sensor as the velocity source, the period meter reads 7/6 high ( tmc9660_units.hpp:178-181 ). Position stays exact. Internal units to calibrate (none of these is documented in the driver): Quantity Hypothesis Calibration step (bench, then frozen into 0x3048) 331/330 packed Iq/Id the same mA scale as ACTUAL_TORQUE without CURRENT_SCALING_FACTOR regress 331.hi against 105 over a torque sweep; store the A/LSB in 0x3048:05 332 packed Ud/Uq, A:305-307, A:314 full scale ±32767 corresponds to OUTPUT_VOLTAGE_LIMIT normalisation open-loop voltage mode at known OPENLOOP_VOLTAGE → compare; store V/LSB at 1 V bus in 0x3048:06 A:311-313, 315 FOC currents ADC-scaled current before mA conversion compare RAMDebug 311 against 105 at a steady state A:333/334 integration period summed per FOC or velocity loop read 333 twice with a known Δt at constant torque OUTPUT_VOLTAGE_LIMIT 32767 = 100 % circular limit sweep in open loop and observe U_dq saturation Until a calibration exists, the OD publishes these quantities as raw I16 with units: raw . docs.text: The cost of one TMCL access on SPI is T_op = 2·T_frame + T_gap + T_post , where T_frame ≈ CS setup + 64 bits at 10 MHz (6.4 µs) + IDF transaction overhead (about 10–15 µs). Measure it; do not assume it. Pipelining: transferTMCL(..., second_command) already lets the second frame of access k carry the command of access k +1, so a batch of N accesses costs about N·(T_gap + T_frame) + T_frame + T_post . Scenario T_gap T_post One access Batch of 6 (pipelined) Batch of 8 A: today ( kTmclPairGapUs , HAL DelayUs(200) ) 1000 µs 200 µs ≈ 1.24 ms ≈ 6.3 ms ≈ 8.4 ms B: conservative 250 µs 0 ≈ 290 µs ≈ 1.6 ms ≈ 2.2 ms C: target 50 µs 0 ≈ 90 µs ≈ 440 µs ≈ 580 µs D: best case (parser keeps up) 10 µs 0 ≈ 50 µs ≈ 200 µs ≈ 260 µs Measurement plan (bench app vortex_tmcl_timing , PR 2b): Instrument HalSpiTmc9660Comm::hostSpiTransferTMCLPair with esp_timer_get_time() around each frame and the gap. Count NOT_READY (0xF0) and 0x00 retries per access. Sweep T_gap ∈ {1000, 500, 250, 100, 50, 25, 10} µs and T_post ∈ {200, 50, 0} µs, in three chip states: SYSTEM_OFF , open-loop current mode at 25 kHz PWM, and FOC (Hall or ABN) under load. Run 10⁵ GAP reads of 125/105/289 at each point. Record the latency histogram (p50/p99/max), the retry count and any value mismatch against a slow reference read. Repeat the chosen point with pipelined batches of 6 and 8. Read G0:12 MAIN_LOOPS in each state. If the TMCL parser is serviced in the chip's main loop, the minimum safe gap tracks 1/ MAIN_LOOPS , so this is the number to report upstream. Pass criterion for a default: 10⁶ accesses with zero corrupt values and p99 retries ≤ 1. Publish the result as the new T_op and update C§4.5. Rules that hold whatever the outcome: Inside drive_rt , a gap longer than about 30 µs must not busy-wait at priority 24. Use a gptimer one-shot plus a task notification, or split the batch across the cycle. The NOT_READY budget inside drive_rt is at most 2 retries. After that the sample is marked stale (0x3041:14 sample age). A stale streak longer than 0x3047:06 cycles raises the "TMC link degraded" cause (§3.3), not a hang. Every TMC access in drive_rt records its latency into 0x3037.
