docs.text: # Finding Evidence Fix (PR 2a) D1 RamDebug::startCapture sends type 6 ( SET_TRIGGER_MASK_SHIFT ) instead of 7 ( ENABLE_TRIGGER ). readData uses opcode ReadMem instead of RamDebug type 9 READ_SAMPLE . getStatus treats any non-zero state as running, but COMPLETE = 3. There is no API for channels, trigger, prescaler or pre-trigger src/tmc9660.ipp:5365-5395 against Table 16/17 in tmc9660_param_mode_tmcl.hpp:330-420 full RAMDebug API ( configure(Channels, Trigger, prescaler, samples, pre) , state() , info(kind) , readSamples(span) ) D2 enum class Parameters includes HEARTBEAT_MONITORING_LIST (ids 3, 4) and HIBERNATION_WAKEUP_LIST (10, 11). These are global bank-0 parameters, and ¾ collide with MOTOR_PWM_FREQUENCY / COMMUTATION_MODE . writeParameter(Parameters::HEARTBEAT_MONITORING_TIMEOUT, 20) would SAP the commutation mode tmc9660_param_mode_tmcl.hpp:5227-5300 ; duplicate-id check in the script remove them from Parameters , keep only GlobalParamBank0 . Add a static_assert for unique axis ids D3 Heartbeat::configureAuto selects TMCL_UART_INTERFACE when enabled. On the SPI-connected Vortex the watchdog would then never see traffic, or would never trip src/tmc9660.ipp:5447-5461 take the interface explicitly. Vortex uses configure(SPI_INTERFACE, 20) D4 Fixed 1000 µs pair gap and 200 µs post-delay. The 10 ms NOT_READY budget suits only thread context tmc9660_comm_interface.hpp transferTMCL ; Tmc9660Handler.cpp:180,201 make gap, post-delay and retry budget per-call parameters. Add readParameters(span<ids>, span<out>) that pipelines D5 Doc comments disagree with the enums ( getMotorContext says NR 8/9/132 for ids 0/1/123). The FOC_ABN report uses other numbers src/tmc9660.ipp:4832-4852 ; TMC9660_FOC_ABN_DEEP_DIVE_REPORT.md §1 the header enums are canonical (they match the 263 OK reads in the post-config scan). Fix the comments D6 134 of 288 axis rows carry no access tag in the driver doc string, and the ADC clip flags have no description Appendix A "RW*" add a 4 th X-macro column ACCESS and a units string. The script then needs no heuristics D7 No wrapper for IPD/HFI sensorless start, index latching or I²t remaining time TMC9660_DEEP_AUDIT_REPORT.md §5 items 8, 9, 11 out of scope here; noted for the roadmap
docs.title: 1.9 Driver defects and gaps found (must fix before relying on them)

docs.text: Before MOTOR_TYPE is set, 259 GAPs return REPLY_WRONG_TYPE . After MOTOR_TYPE = BLDC , 263 axis parameters read OK ( TMCL_PARAM_SCAN_POST_CONFIG.md ). The apply order must therefore set the motor type first. Telemetry must not start until the image has been applied. NR 181–201 (SPI encoder) and 205–209 (step/dir) return REPLY_CMD_NOT_AVAILABLE unless the bootloader enables them. Gaps at 86-88, 158-160, 179-180, 200 and 215 are not parameters. NR 230 is write-only. The ROM rejects Y2 and VGS-short on/off writes on the 3-phase build, NR 245/246 gate currents ( INVALID_VALUE ), and I²t time constants below about 1 s ( vortex_bench_safety.hpp , I²t comment). The default UVW VGS-short protection false-trips on Vortex, so the bench disables it ( disable_vortex_uvw_vgs_short_protection , vortex_motor_bench_common.hpp:830 ). Erratum 4: target updates are serviced in a ~1 kHz loop ( vortex_bench_safety.hpp:169-173 ). AS5047U ABI → TMC ABN1 is a working bench path ( vortex_bldc_abn_as5047_dynamics.cpp:6-48 , 14-bit ABI = 16384 counts/rev). This partly answers C-Q5. It needs the ABN1 bootloader mux and the physical wiring.

docs.title: 2.1 Tiers

docs.text: Each cycle has three kinds of slots: Fixed slots (always, in a pipelined batch): (1) SAP of the active target, (2) GAP position or velocity actual by mode (csp/pp → 144, csv/pv → 125, cst/tq → 331), (3) GAP 331 (Iq/Id) unless (2) already was 331, (4) GAP 289 status, (5) GAP 299/300 alternating (error words are fresh every 2 cycles), (6) AS5047U frame (host SPI, not TMCL). That is 5 TMCL accesses. Rotating slots (default R = 2 per cycle): a static, precomputed table serves the F/S/H tiers. At 500 Hz, R = 2 gives 1000 accesses/s: for example 10 F signals × 50 Hz = 500, 21 S signals × 10 Hz = 210, 10 H signals × 1 Hz = 10, with 280 to spare. The table is generated at transition 3 from 0x3047 and the selected feedback (no Hall reads when Hall is unused). A FAULTN edge (PCAL95555 GPIO_PCAL_TMC_FAULT_STATUS → INT → i2c_io ) preempts the rotation: on the next cycle the rotating slots read 299, 300 and 301. Service slot (S = 2 per cycle in Operation Enabled, up to 16 otherwise): configuration apply and verify, RAMDebug arm/poll/readout, on-demand SDO GAPs (an SDO read of 0x3044:xx outside the scope), and the 0x4100 bridge. Required SPI time per cycle = (5 + R + S)·(T_gap + T_frame) + T_frame + AS5047U ≈ 9·(T_gap + 20) + 35 µs. Scenario SPI time / cycle Max SYNC rate with SPI ≤ 50 % of cycle Recommended A (today) ≈ 9.2 ms ≈ 55 Hz not usable for cyclic modes. Profile modes at 10 ms with R = 0, S = 1 B ≈ 2.5 ms ≈ 200 Hz 100–200 Hz C ≈ 665 µs ≈ 750 Hz 500 Hz (C§4.5 default) D ≈ 305 µs ≈ 1.6 kHz (capped at 1 kHz by Erratum 4) 1 kHz When the cycle cannot fit R + S, drive_rt drops service work first, then rotating slots. It never drops fixed slots. It counts each drop in 0x3037:09/10. The scheduler is a pure function in contracts ( TelemetrySchedule Build(Rates, Feedback, Mode, BudgetUs) ), which host tests cover.
docs.title: 2.2 drive_rt SPI schedule

docs.text: drive_rt publishes a TelemetryFrame (about 160 B) through a seqlock, one per cycle. Every value carries the cycle number of its last successful read, so consumers know its age. 0x3041:14 is the age in cycles of the oldest fixed-slot value. TPDOs read the frame from the previous cycle, as C§4.4 specifies. SDO od_extensions copy the frame and convert it to SI (R32) on read, outside drive_rt .

docs.text: One interface, two engines. 0x4300:03 selects the engine. Both write the same capture format into one RAM buffer, so the tools never need to know which engine produced a capture. Property Host engine (H) TMC engine (T, RAMDebug) Sample clock drive_rt cycle (SYNC or gptimer), × decimation 1..65535 RAMDebug frequency ( GET_INFO 2) / (prescaler + 1) Sources any PDO-mappable OD object, any TMC parameter (an extra access per cycle each, admitted only if it fits the budget), host signals: demand values, following error, controlword/statusword, AS5047U angle/velocity/AGC, IMU (sample-and-hold of the 100–400 Hz i2c_io snapshot), SYNC jitter, RT step time TMC axis and global parameters only (channel type ⅓) Channels ≤ 8 ≤ GET_INFO 0 (query at boot, store in 0x4303:05) Depth K = RAM / (4·N): 32 KiB default → 1024 samples × 8 ch, 4096 × 2 ch ≤ GET_INFO 1 words total (shared by channels) Trigger level (rising/falling/either, with hysteresis), bit-mask edge (status words), fault (any FaultBook activation), controlword edge (set-point ack, mode change), manual, external input (spare GPIO) unconditional, rising/falling/dual signed or unsigned threshold, on a channel with mask/shift ( SET_TRIGGER_MASK_SHIFT ) Pre-trigger 0..K−1 samples SET_PRETRIGGER_COUNT Readout no SPI READ_SAMPLE in the service slot, one access per 32-bit word. 4 ch × 512 samples = 2048 accesses: ≈ 2 s at S = 2 and 500 Hz in Operation Enabled, ≈ 0.25 s idle with S = 16 in scenario C Source identifiers are U32 values written into 0x4301:1..8: Bits 31–28 Class Bits 27–0 1 TMC axis parameter axis<<16 | parameter id 2 TMC global parameter bank<<16 | id 3 OD object index<<8 | sub 4 host internal signal enum ( demand_pos , demand_vel , demand_torque , following_error , sync_jitter_us , rt_step_us , cw , sw , …) 5 AS5047U field (angle raw, compensated, velocity, AGC, magnitude, error flags) 6 IMU field (quaternion i/j/k/r, accel xyz, gyro xyz, mag xyz) The Python package generates the source catalog from the OD YAML and the inventory, so names, units and scales are not stored on the device. The device exposes only a catalog hash (0x4303:09) to detect mismatches. State machine (0x4300:02): IDLE → ARMED (pre-trigger filling) → TRIGGERED → COMPLETE , plus READOUT (TMC engine copying the chip buffer into node RAM) and ERROR (0x4300:10 reason: budget, source unavailable, RAMDebug reply code). Commands (0x4300:01): 1 arm, 2 force trigger, 3 stop, 4 reset, 5 re-arm automatically after readout (rolling mode for the live phase-current panel). Capture format (0x4302 DOMAIN, little-endian): header { u32 magic 'VXSC'; u16 version=1; u8 engine; u8 n_ch; u32 n_samples; u32 trigger_index; u32 pre_samples; u32 sample_period_ns; u64 t0_uptime_us; u64 t0_time_ms (CiA TIME-synced); u16 trigger_cause; u16 flags (bit0 wrapped, bit1 stale samples present) } channel { u32 source_id; u8 type (I16/I32/U16/U32/R32); u8 unit (CiA 303-2 code); u16 reserved; f32 scale_to_si; f32 offset } x n_ch data sample-major, n_samples x n_ch values, ring unrolled to start at oldest sample crc32 over header+channel+data The block upload runs at ≥ 20 kB/s (bench test B3), so a 32 KiB capture takes about 1.6 s on CAN and is near-instant over the Wi-Fi tunnel. The upload is served from the frozen buffer. A new arm is refused with abort 0x08000022 while an upload is in progress. RAM budget on the C6: scope buffer 32 KiB (Kconfig VORTEX_SCOPE_RAM_KB , 8–64), fault-snapshot rings 2 × 8 KiB, TelemetryFrame and seqlock 0.5 KiB, schedule tables 1 KiB. Total ≈ 50 KiB, allocated once at boot from internal RAM and never freed. If Wi-Fi is enabled and free heap at boot drops below 64 KiB after allocation, the scope buffer shrinks to 16 KiB and 0x4303:03 reports the actual size.
docs.title: 2.5 Scope engine

docs.text: Cycle-rate ring: 8 fixed channels, I16 scaled (Iq, Id, Vbus, velocity, position low word, demand, statusword, TMC error summary), 1024 samples. At 500 Hz that is 2.05 s. drive_rt writes it every cycle in about 1 µs. Freeze: when FaultBook activates a cause of class Fault or Disable-now, the ring records 0x4310:02 post-trigger milliseconds (default 200), then freezes into slot 0 (latest) and, the first time after boot, also into slot 1. A frozen snapshot cannot be overwritten until it is read or cleared (0x4310:01 = 3). The journal entry (C§6.4) gets the snapshot sequence number. PWM-rate black box: while the user scope is idle, the TMC engine stays armed in fault-capture mode. Channels are 311/312/313 (FOC currents), 305 (U voltage) and 300 (GDRV flags). The trigger channel is 300, rising unsigned with threshold 0 and mask 0xFFFFFFFF. Pre-trigger is 75 %. On a gate-driver fault the chip itself holds the waveforms around the event. After the drive has stopped, drive_rt reads them out in the service slot into slot 2 of 0x4311. (Verify on the bench that a channel can trigger on parameter 300 and that RAMDebug keeps running after the fault handler has stopped the bridge.) Policy 0x4310:04 decides whether a user capture may pre-empt the black box (default yes, and the dashboard shows that the black box is off). Persistence: a snapshot is written to NVS vortex_log only outside Operation Enabled, which is the journal rule (C§4.4). Each record is ≤ 8 KiB, and one is kept. The readout is 0x4311 DOMAIN in the §2.5 format with engine = 2 (cycle snapshot) or 3 (black box). 0x4312 lists the slots (sequence number, time, cause, size).

docs.text:
flowchart TB B["board 0x2901
ESP32 die temp, heap, reset reason,
thread liveness, NVS, TMC identity"] --> P["power 0x2902
Vbus, OV/UV warn, PCAL power-good,
VDRV/gdrv supply UV, brake chopper, NTC"] P --> G["gate driver 0x2903 (rollup) / 0x3031
OC per phase+side, VGS shorts,
bootstrap UV, retries"] G --> M["motor 0x2904 / 0x3032
I2t, chip temp, current clipping,
regulation state, following error"] M --> F["feedback 0x2905 / 0x3033
Hall, ABN init, SPI enc, AS5047U,
angle plausibility, IMU"] B --> C["comms 0x2906
CAN TEC/REC, bus-off, HB consumer, SYNC,
RPDO timeout, TMC SPI link, wireless"] The ordering expresses causality for the "root-cause" view. A child's fault is shown as caused by the parent when the parent faulted in the same or the previous cycle. For example, bootstrap undervoltage during a Vbus sag is attributed to power, not the gate driver. Each node is a RECORD with the same layout: Sub Name Type Meaning 1 status U8 0 unknown, 1 ok, 2 warning, 3 fault, 4 not fitted / disabled 2 active causes U32 bitmask of this node's cause ids (node-local numbering, decoded by the tool) 3 latched causes U32 OR since the last clear (write 0 to clear) 4 fault count U32 number of Fault-class activations since boot 5 warning count U32 6 last EMCY code U16 7 last event uptime U32 ms 8 worst value I32 node-specific (max temperature 0.1 °C, min Vbus 0.1 V, max I²t %, max following error, max TEC) 9 worst value uptime U32 ms 0x2900 is the summary: sub1–6 hold the node statuses, sub7 is a U32 packed rollup (4 bits per node, PDO-mappable, sent on change) and sub8 clears all latches (write 0x726C6300 ). Gate driver, motor and feedback are per axis (0x3031–0x3033). 0x2903–0x2905 are the worst-of over all axes. Per-bit counters: 0x3034 ARRAY U16[32] counts rising edges of each GENERAL_ERROR_FLAGS bit, 0x3035 U16[32] does the same for GDRV_ERROR_FLAGS and 0x3036 U16[14] for ADC_STATUS_FLAGS . They saturate at 65535 and reset on 0x2900:08. TMC link statistics are in 0x3037 (accesses, failures by reply code, NOT_READY retries, stale samples, max latency µs, latency histogram, configured gap, slot drops).

docs.title: 3.3 Extensions to the fault policy table (C§6.4)

docs.text:
flowchart LR CAT["catalog row 0x3000"] --> ENG["engineering layer 0x3001-0x3009
(SI: A, Ohm, H, Hz, V, degC)"] COM["commissioning results 0x3022
(accept)"] --> ENG ENG -->|"derive (pure, contracts)"| IMG["TMC image 0x3100-0x3112
(TMC units)"] PIN["pin mask 0x3120
(expert overrides)"] --> IMG IMG -->|"apply at transition 3"| CHIP["TMC9660 RAM"] CHIP -->|"read-back"| VER["verify 0x3019"] The engineering layer is the user's view. It keeps the CANopen design's 0x3001–0x3009 objects, refined to carry the extra nameplate data the derivation needs: Rs, Ls, Kt, J (optional), peak and continuous current, shunt, FET Qg/Rds(on), target current-loop bandwidth. The TMC image is the chip's view. It is generated from the header (one sub-index per TMC parameter, §6.2). derive(Eng, BoardFacts, QuirkProfile) → Image is a pure function in contracts/tmc_image.hpp . It contains the driver's auto-config math ( CurrentSensing::configureAuto gain choice, GateDriver power-stage profile, Protection::configureAuto I²t and threshold encoding, Ramp k_rpm/acceleration conversion). The firmware therefore no longer calls the driver's configureAuto helpers at runtime. It applies a precomputed image. Host tests cover the math. Pinning: 0x3120 is an ARRAY U32[19], one bitmask per image object. A set bit means "keep the user's value and do not re-derive it". Any SDO write to an image sub-index sets its pin bit automatically. params unpin <obj> clears it. The parameter editor (§5.3) shows pinned values with a marker. Persistence: both layers persist in group A ( od_app ). Calibration-type results (Hall offsets, ABN N-offset, ADC offsets once accepted) persist in group K. The image is saved too, so a DCF reproduces a drive exactly even if a later firmware changes the derivation. On restore with a newer firmware, un-pinned sub-indices are re-derived and pinned ones are kept.
docs.title: 4.1 Two layers, one truth

docs.text: Writes are validated in two passes: On SDO write (od_extension): data type, the YAML low / high range and access. Violations abort 0x06090031/0x06090032/0x06090030, as C§6.2 specifies. At transition 3 , over the whole image. The failure code goes to 0x3019:03 and the first offending object/sub-index to 0x3019:04. The transition is refused with EMCY 0x6320. Code Rule 0x01 range: every image value inside the inventory range (Appendix A) 0x02 MAX_TORQUE (6) ≤ min(board limit, catalog peak, 0x6073 · rated). MAX_FLUX (7) ≥ OPENLOOP_CURRENT (46) whenever an open-loop or forced-φe ABN init is configured ( vortex_bench_safety.hpp kMaxFluxCurrentMa note) 0x03 supply: UV warn (292) < nominal < OV warn (291) < brake-chopper limit (213) + hysteresis (214) < board absolute maximum 0x04 temperature: warning < shutdown for chip (298/297) and external (295/294); external thresholds converted from °C with the NTC curve 0x05 I²t: time constants ≥ 1000 ms (ROM floor); limit 1 ≥ limit 2 scaled by time (window 1 is the shorter one) 0x06 PWM 10–100 kHz; OUTPUT_VOLTAGE_LIMIT ≤ 32767; dead time (235/236) ≥ the FET requirement from 0x3002 0x07 feedback: the commutation mode, velocity sensor (123) and position sensor (142) must each be fitted (status b27–b29 availability) and muxed by the bootloader ( DeviceCapabilities , the BootloaderConfig board fact). ABN STEPS > 0 when ABN is selected. SPI-encoder sub-indices only if spiEncoder 0x08 Y2: no Y2 sub-index differs from the default when y2Phase = false (Vortex) 0x09 quirk profile (keyed by TMC FW id in 0x2002): skip NR 245/246 on FW051V100 unless the user pinned them and set 0x3121:03 "allow"; VGS-short UVW policy (disable or max deglitch) applied 0x0A position: limit low < limit high; POSITION_REACHED_THRESHOLD consistent with 0x6067 0x0B ramp: RAMP_VMAX ≥ the motor-side speed implied by 0x607F and the gear ratio; RAMP_VSTOP ≥ 1 0x0C heartbeat: config = SPI; timeout ≥ 3 × the idle drive_rt period and ≤ 50 ms 0x0D globals: AUTO_START_ENABLE = 0, CLEAR_USER_VARIABLES = 1 0x0E verify mismatch (§4.4) 0x0F TMCL error during apply (the reply code goes to 0x3019:05)
docs.title: 4.2 Validation rules

docs.text: The order follows the proven bench sequence ( BENCH_MATRIX.md "TMC9660 BLDC bring-up shape", configure_complete_bldc ) and the firmware facts in §1.10. It runs in the drive_rt service slot with S raised to 16 accesses per cycle, because the bridge is off. The statusword stays in Ready to Switch On until the apply finishes. 0x3019:01 shows progress. Step Writes Notes 0 read G2:15 epoch, error b9, FW id decides between full and differential apply (§4.5) 1 A:4 = SYSTEM_OFF 2 0x3100 motor (type first , then pole pairs, direction, PWM, scheme, idle behaviour, voltage limit) before the motor type is set, most other parameters answer WRONG_TYPE 3 0x3101 gate driver (UVW only, quirk skips) 4 0x3102 protection (UVLO, OC, VGS) Vortex VGS policy 5 0x3103 current sensing 6 0x3108–0x310B the selected feedback only 7 0x3104 current loop, 0x3105 velocity loop, 0x3106 position loop, 0x310C biquads 8 0x3107 ramp and open-loop 9 0x310D protection (supply warnings, temperatures, I²t, fault handling) 10 0x310E brake, 0x310F stop events/switches, 0x3110 reference search, 0x3111 step/dir 11 0x3112 globals (SGP): heartbeat SPI + timeout last among the globals, so that a slow apply does not trip it 12 clear error/gdrv/ADC flags (write-1-clear all) 13 ADC offset calibration if status b11 = 0 (motor stationary) 14 read-back verify (§4.4) 15 write G2:15 = CRC32(image) epoch token Transition 4 then writes the target to zero, sets DRV_EN (PCAL), sets the commutation mode and reads back A:4 and status b0–b3 within 20 ms, else Fault 0xFF50. That is the C§5.6 behaviour plus the revert check. Time estimate: about 230 writes + 230 reads + flag clears ≈ 470 accesses. Scenario A: ≈ 0.6 s. Scenario C with S = 16 at 500 Hz: ≈ 60 ms.
docs.title: 4.3 Apply order at transition 3

docs.text: Every RW/RWE sub-index that was written is read back with GAP/GGP. Write-only parameters (230) and RWC latches are skipped. A tolerance table covers parameters that the chip rounds or normalises. For example, MOTOR_PWM_FREQUENCY is accepted within ±1 % (verify which parameters are rounded by observing them on the bench, and record them in the quirk profile). The result is in 0x3019: verified count, mismatch count, first mismatch (index, sub, wanted, got) and the TMCL reply code. A mismatch refuses transition 3 (code 0x0E). diag config and the parameter editor show the full mismatch list, which the tool fetches by re-reading 0x3100–0x3112 against the stored image.
docs.title: 4.4 Read-back verification

docs.text: G2:15 (a TMCL-script user variable that Vortex does not need for scripts) holds the CRC32 of the last applied image. CLEAR_USER_VARIABLES = 1 makes the chip clear it on reset. At the next transition 3: If G2:15 = CRC(last applied), WATCHDOG_EVENT = 0 and the chip has not been reset (no bootloader re-entry since the last apply), then only the sub-indices that changed since the last apply are written and verified. This is typically a few gains during tuning, which keeps tuning iterations under 50 ms. Otherwise the full apply runs. A mismatch that appears while the drive is enabled means the TMC reset under us: Fault 0x6010 (§3.3).
docs.title: 4.5 Differential apply and TMC reset detection

docs.text: Export ( params export dcf FILE ): python-canopen uploads every object whose YAML persist is app , cal or comm . That includes the image and the pin masks. It writes a CiA 306 DCF with [DeviceComissioning] (node-ID, bit-rate, node name). Comments record the OD hash (0x5FFE), the firmware build (0x2000) and the TMC FW id (0x2002). The library function is canopen.objectdictionary.export_od(od, f, doc_type="dcf") . Import ( params import dcf FILE [--store] ): this refuses unless the drive is in Pre-operational or Switched On and holds authority (C§6.6). It checks the OD hash. If the hash differs, it maps by (index, sub, name) and reports dropped entries, which is the same rule as the TLV restore (C§6.7). It writes the engineering layer, then the pin masks, then the pinned image sub-indices. It optionally calls 0x1010:03/:04. Diff: the device exposes the stored TLV blobs read-only as 0x2801:01–03 DOMAIN (comm/app/cal). The tool decodes them with the same codec as the firmware (the Python port is shared in the package and tested against C++ fixtures). It then shows three columns: live / stored / default (from the EDS). The dashboard parameter editor uses the same data.
docs.title: 4.6 DCF export and import, diff against stored and defaults

docs.text: The OD is the single truth. The chip is reprogrammed at every transition 3 (C§6.1). Storing on the chip would create a second truth that could diverge silently. NvmStorage::storeToFlash (STAP 0xFFF) needs external SPI flash or I²C EEPROM configured through the bootloader ( inc/tmc9660.hpp NvmStorage warning). The Vortex SPI boot configuration has enable_flash = false , so the SPI port stays free for TMCL ( TMCL_PARAM_SCAN_POST_CONFIG.md table). Enforcement: STAP, FactoryDefault and the script opcodes are refused by the 0x4100 bridge unless a build flag VORTEX_TMC_EXPERT is set. At boot, status b5 CONFIG_LOADED = 1 raises the "unexpected TMC NVM config" warning, because someone used the vendor tool on this board. AUTO_START_ENABLE = 0 guarantees that no stored script runs.
docs.title: 4.7 TMC9660 non-volatile memory is not used

docs.text: Command Function Data path plot SIG... [--profile diag|tune-*] [--rate] [--csv F] live plot of named signals (the catalog resolves names to OD, scale and units). Applies the matching PDO profile temporarily and restores the mapping on exit TPDO scope arm --engine host|tmc --ch iq,id,uq,ud --trigger 'iq>1.5A rising' --pre 25% --samples 2048 --decim 1 , scope wait , scope fetch -o cap.vxsc , scope show cap.vxsc [--fft --cursors] , scope export --csv|--parquet the scope engine (§2.5) SDO + block upload scope rolling --ch iu,iv,iw re-arm loop for live phase currents (TMC engine) as above diag tree [--watch] health tree with statuses, latches, counters and worst values. Shows root-cause attribution SDO 0x2900–0x2906, 0x3031–0x3037 diag flags [--watch] decoded TMC status/error/gdrv/ADC words, with the bit names generated from the inventory 0x3030 diag snapshot list|fetch|clear fault snapshots and the PWM-rate black box 0x4310–0x4312 diag link TMCL latency histogram, retries, stale counts, slot drops; CAN statistics; SYNC jitter 0x3037, 0x4201, 0x4202 diag config apply/verify status and the mismatch list 0x3019, 0x3100–0x3112 tune current [--bw 1kHz] [--step 0.5A] [--apply] derive Kp/Ki from R, L and the bandwidth (C§6.3 step 7). flowchart LR subgraph PY["vortex-canopen dash (Python)"] NET["NodeSession
(python-canopen Network, one per bus)"] HUB["SignalHub
TPDO decode -> named SI signals,
ring per signal (60 s)"] JOB["SdoJobQueue
(one SDO client per node, serialised)"] API["FastAPI app
REST /api/* WS /ws/stream"] end BUS["python-can bus
(USB-CAN / tls:// / pipe)"] <--> NET NET --> HUB --> API JOB <--> NET API <--> JOB UI["browser SPA (static, packaged)
Svelte + uPlot + three.js"] <-->|"WS msgpack 30 Hz batches"| API Backend: FastAPI on uvicorn, bound to 127.0.0.1 by default. A random session token is printed in the URL and checked on REST and WebSocket. There is one NodeSession per bus, and it uses the same transport options as the CLI ( --interface/--channel or --url ). SignalHub subscribes to TPDO callbacks and to EMCY/heartbeat. It decodes values with the catalog and pushes them to subscribed clients in 33 ms batches (msgpack: {sig_id: [t0, dt, values...]} ). SdoJobQueue serialises SDO jobs (snapshot polls, scope fetches, parameter reads/writes) with priorities, so a 32 KiB block upload cannot starve the 2 Hz health poll. Frontend: a static single-page app built at release time and shipped inside the wheel (no Node.js at install). It uses Svelte for the UI, uPlot ( https://github.com/leeoniya/uPlot ) for all time-series and FFT plots (it renders tens of thousands of points per frame), and three.js for the IMU attitude. Library versions are pinned in package-lock.json . The bundle must work offline. Safety: without --allow-control the dashboard is read-only. Commands that can move the motor (wizard steps, enable, tune steps) are hidden. The server refuses any write to 0x6040, 0x3020, 0x3023 or 0x3100–0x3112. With --allow-control , motion buttons need a confirmation and use the same authority rules as the CLI (C§7.4). The page shows a persistent "control enabled" banner and a large quick-stop button that writes 0x6040 = quick stop. Recording: any panel can record to Parquet (signals plus EMCY/state events) via a toolbar button. The recordings replay in the same UI ( dash --replay FILE ).

docs.text: The keys are the C§4.2 attributes: name (ParameterName), object_type (VAR/ARRAY/RECORD/DOMAIN), data_type , access , pdo_mapping , default , low / high , units , persist ( comm|app|cal|none ), od_extension , fd_only and docs . The fragment adds two keys, which odgen must learn: tmc: {bank: axis|0|2, id: N} binds a sub-index to a TMC parameter. The TmcParamGroup / TmcTelemetry extensions use it to find the parameter. tmcl_inventory.py --check uses it to prove coverage. source: snapshot|service|ram says where an od_extension serves the value from. snapshot means the drive_rt seqlock frame, with no SPI on read. service means a GAP in the service slot, so the SDO response is deferred. ram means node RAM. Sub-index 0 of RECORD and ARRAY objects is implicit (highest sub-index), as in CANopenNode v4. Names are snake_case. odgen derives the ParameterName from them. pdo_mapping: true is only set where the classic 8-byte limit allows a useful mapping. The indices are for axis 1. The generator replicates the axis objects at +0x400 per axis.

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs hardfoc-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Four tasks over one HAL ¶ Four tasks over one HAL Figure description and sources From top to bottom. The ESP-IDF main task runs app_main, which starts the VortexSys orchestrator task and waits for its boot table, then becomes the supervisor loop. VortexSys brings up the HAL, starts the LedDemo thread (WS2812TestThread) and, when menuconfig selects the CANopen device, the co_svc task that serves CoNode (CANopenNode over the generated object dictionary, on the TWAI port). Every task reaches the hardware through the Vortex HAL singleton, which owns the managers, the hf-core handlers and the chip drivers. Stack sizes and priorities are the constants in the sources listed below. docs.text: Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs hardfoc-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from.

docs.text: Four tasks over one HAL Figure description and sources From top to bottom. The ESP-IDF main task runs app_main, which starts the VortexSys orchestrator task and waits for its boot table, then becomes the supervisor loop. VortexSys brings up the HAL, starts the LedDemo thread (WS2812TestThread) and, when menuconfig selects the CANopen device, the co_svc task that serves CoNode (CANopenNode over the generated object dictionary, on the TWAI port). Every task reaches the hardware through the Vortex HAL singleton, which owns the managers, the hf-core handlers and the chip drivers. Stack sizes and priorities are the constants in the sources listed below. docs.text: USB-CAN tools ¶ Python scripts that send CANopen NMT and expedited SDO frames from a PC through a USB-CAN adapter, for bench checks. The scripts build frames by hand with python-can, with the same COB-IDs as hf-core's hf-utils-canopen ( canopen_frames.py ): NMT 0x000 , SDO request 0x600 + node , SDO response 0x580 + node . They are not part of the firmware build. The CANopen node design plans to replace them with the vortex-canopen package, which reads the generated EDS. A valid sequence moves a drive ds402_velocity_demo walks a CiA 402 drive to Operation Enabled. Use a current-limited supply, no load and a known node ID. Install ¶ cd docs/tools/usb-can python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt requirements.txt installs python-can. The adapter needs a python-can interface : socketcan on Linux ( --channel can0 ); slcan , pcan or usb2can on Windows, depending on the adapter. Scripts ¶ Script What it does test_frame_encoding.py Checks the frame builders offline; no adapter needed ds402_host_test.py --action nmt_start Sends NMT Start to the node ds402_host_test.py --action read_status Reads the statusword 0x6041 by SDO (the default action) ds402_host_test.py --action ds402_velocity_demo NMT Start, the CiA 402 enable sequence ( 0x6040 = 6, 7, 15), profile velocity mode and a target velocity of 100 Option Default Meaning --interface socketcan python-can interface name --channel can0 Interface channel, for example COM5 for slcan --bitrate 500000 Nominal bit rate; the firmware uses 500 kbit/s --node-id 1 Target node; the firmware default is 1 --timeout 0.5 Seconds to wait for each SDO reply python3 test_frame_encoding.py python3 ds402_host_test.py --interface socketcan --channel can0 --node-id 1 --action read_status With the CANopen device selected, the node answers on its node-ID (default 1). It waits in pre-operational for an NMT start ( CANopen ).
